212	    /// Opens each file through the core. Off the main thread: a file can be large.
213	    static func readTracks(_ files: [UInt32: URL]) throws -> [UInt32: ReelCursor] {
214	        var tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor] = [:]
215	        for (media, file) in files {
216	            do {
217	                tracks[media] = try ReelCursor(data: try Data(contentsOf: file))
218	            } catch {
219	                let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
220	                throw Refusal(
221	                    message: "The cursor file \(file.lastPathComponent) could not be read: "
222	                        + reason)
223	            }
224	        }
225	        return tracks
226	    }
227	
228	    /// Whether any file holds a typing stretch (CU-25's `typing` events).
229	    static func hasTyping(_ tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor]) -> Bool {
230	        let request = #"{"events":{"from":0,"to":4611686018427387903,"kinds":["typing"]}}"#
231	        return tracks.values.contains { track in
232	            guard let text = try? track.query(request),
233	                let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))
234	                    as? [String: Any]
235	            else { return false }
236	            return !((object["typing"] as? [Any]) ?? []).isEmpty
237	        }
238	    }
239	
240	    /// `plan_zooms`' request JSON for `clips` (container ticks `from`/`to`, nil for none).
241	    static func request(
242	        _ clips: [UInt32], settings: AutoZoomSettings, from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
243	    ) -> String {
244	        var args: [String: Any] = [
245	            "clips": clips.map { Int($0) }, "zoom": settings.zoom, "lead": settings.lead,
246	            "stay": settings.stay, "follow": settings.follow, "typing": settings.typing,
247	            "replace": settings.replace,
248	        ]
249	        if let from { args["from"] = from }
250	        if let to { args["to"] = to }
251	        let data = (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ["plan_zooms": args])) ?? Data()
252	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
253	    }
254	
255	    /// Asks the core for the plan over `clips` of `project` (the edited one, so inside a nest
256	    /// the nest's), one track per clip; throws the core's sentence as a `Refusal`.
257	    static func plan(
258	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor], project: ReelProject,
259	        settings: AutoZoomSettings, from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
260	    ) throws -> AutoZoomPlan {
261	        var ordered: [ReelCursor] = []
262	        for clip in clips {
263	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source, let track = tracks[id] else {
264	                throw Refusal(message: "Clip \(clip.id)'s cursor file was not read.")
265	            }
266	            ordered.append(track)
267	        }
268	        let text: String
269	        do {
270	            text = try ReelCursor.query(
271	                request(clips.map(\.id), settings: settings, from: from, to: to),
272	                tracks: ordered, project: project)
273	        } catch {
274	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
275	            throw Refusal(message: sentence(reason))
276	        }
277	        guard let answer = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))
278	            as? [String: Any]
279	        else { throw Refusal(message: "Auto Zoom's plan could not be read.") }
280	        var ops = try ((answer["ops"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []).map(op)
281	        func count(_ key: String) -> Int { (answer[key] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0 }
282	        let actions = (answer["actions"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []
283	        let blurred = unblurred(actions, in: project.snapshot)
284	        if settings.motionBlur > 0, !blurred.isEmpty {
285	            ops.append(
286	                .setVideo(clips: blurred, patch: VideoPatch(motionBlur: settings.motionBlur)))
287	        }
288	        return AutoZoomPlan(
289	            ops: ops, visits: count("visits"), added: count("added"),
290	            replaced: count("replaced"), dropped: count("dropped"),
291	            closedAtCut: count("closed_at_cut"), basesSet: count("bases_set"),
292	            actions: actions, blurred: settings.motionBlur > 0 ? blurred.count : 0)
293	    }
294	
295	    /// The distinct clips the planned actions name, in first-named order, whose BASE
296	    /// `video.motion_blur` is 0 (CU-118 (c)): a clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
297	    private static func unblurred(_ actions: [[String: Any]], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
298	        -> [UInt32]
299	    {
300	        var clips: [UInt32] = []
301	        for action in actions {
302	            guard let id = (action["clip"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value, !clips.contains(id),
303	                let clip = snapshot.clip(id), (clip.video?.motionBlur ?? 0) <= 0
304	            else { continue }
305	            clips.append(id)
306	        }
307	        return clips
308	    }
309	
310	    /// The core's lowercase sentence as one a person reads: capitalised, with a full stop.
311	    static func sentence(_ core: String) -> String {
312	        guard let first = core.first else { return core }
313	        let text = first.uppercased() + core.dropFirst()
314	        return text.hasSuffix(".") ? text : text + "."
315	    }
316	
317	    /// One op of the answer, through `ReelOps.swift`'s factories.
318	    private static func op(_ o: [String: Any]) throws -> ReelOp {
319	        func id(_ key: String) -> UInt32 { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0 }
320	        func ticks(_ key: String) -> Ticks { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value ?? 0 }
321	        switch o["op"] as? String {
322	        case "remove_action":
323	            return .removeAction(clip: id("clip"), action: id("action"))
324	        case "set_video":
325	            let clips = ((o["clips"] as? [NSNumber]) ?? []).map(\.uint32Value)
326	            return .setVideoRaw(clips: clips, patch: o["patch"] ?? [String: Any]())
327	        case "add_zoom_action":
328	            return .addZoomActionRaw(
329	                clip: id("clip"), at: ticks("at"), duration: ticks("duration"),
330	                region: o["region"] ?? NSNull(),
331	                fit: (o["fit"] as? String).flatMap(ZoomFit.init(rawValue:)),
332	                curve: (o["curve"] as? String).flatMap(Curve.init(rawValue:)))
333	        default:
334	            throw Refusal(message: "Auto Zoom's plan named an op it does not make.")
335	        }
336	    }
337	}

3	/// Add Shortcut Overlays' Swift half (road map "creator-jobs" CU8, spec §11 CU-80…CU-84): the
4	/// settings, the bundled `keyboard-keys` template and the module rule (CU-81), and
5	/// `plan_overlays` asked of the core through `ReelCursor` (this file names no `rc_*`, CJ-8 (l))
6	/// with its answer read into ops. Both doors — Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays
7	/// (`EditorViewController+ShortcutOverlays.swift`) and `add_shortcut_overlays`
8	/// (`AgentServer+ShortcutOverlays.swift`) — place through `prepared`. The cursor files are
9	/// found and read by `AutoZoom.cursorFiles` and `AutoZoom.readTracks`.
10	
11	/// What a run places with (CU-80's defaults; the owner's answer: bottom, dark). Nothing is
12	/// remembered: the menu item has no sheet to change it.
13	struct ShortcutOverlaySettings: Equatable {
14	    var duration = 1.5
15	    var position = "bottom"
16	    var theme = "dark"
17	
18	    static let durationRange: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.5...10
19	    static let positions = ["bottom", "center", "top"]
20	    static let themes = ["dark", "light"]
21	}

23	/// `plan_overlays`' answer: the ops in the core's order and its counts.
24	struct ShortcutOverlayPlan {
25	    let ops: [ReelOp]
26	    let added, dropped, merged: Int
27	    let track: UInt32
28	    let newTrack: Bool
29	    let overlays: [[String: Any]]
30	}

32	enum ShortcutOverlays {
33	    /// The undo step's name, both doors.
34	    static let actionName = "Add Shortcut Overlays"
35	    /// The bundled template the overlays are drawn by.
36	    static let templateName = "keyboard-keys"
37	
38	    /// What a run that placed nothing says (CU-84).
39	    static let nothingSentence =
40	        "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added."
41	
42	    /// What a run that dropped `n` presses says (CU-80).
43	    static func droppedSentence(_ n: Int) -> String {
44	        n == 1
45	            ? "1 shortcut came too close to show."
46	            : "\(n) shortcuts came too close to show."
47	    }
48	
49	    /// The documents a menu run is reading cursor files for. Main only.
50	    private static var pending: Set<ObjectIdentifier> = []
51	
52	    static func isPending(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
53	        pending.contains(ObjectIdentifier(document))
54	    }
55	
56	    static func setPending(_ document: ProjectDocument, _ on: Bool) {
57	        if on {
58	            pending.insert(ObjectIdentifier(document))
59	        } else {
60	            pending.remove(ObjectIdentifier(document))
61	        }
62	    }

64	    /// The bundled `keyboard-keys.js`: its URL, its bytes and the schema
65	    /// `GraphicTemplateLibrary` compiled from it. Main (the library's first read).
66	    static func template() throws -> (url: URL, bytes: Data, schema: [String: Any]) {
67	        guard let found = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: templateName) else {
68	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(
69	                message: "The bundled \(templateName) template is missing from this build.")
70	        }
71	        guard case .compiled(_, _, _, let schema) = found.entry,
72	            let bytes = try? Data(contentsOf: found.template.url)
73	        else {
74	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(
75	                message: "The bundled \(templateName) template does not compile.")
76	        }
77	        return (found.template.url, bytes, schema)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// CU-81: a module of `store` whose bytes equal the template's — `keyboard-keys` first,
81	    /// else the lowest name — or nil.
82	    static func reusableModule(in store: GraphicStore, bytes: Data) -> String? {
83	        let same = store.scan.modules.values.filter { $0.bytes == bytes }.map(\.name)
84	        return same.contains(templateName) ? templateName : same.min()
85	    }
86	
87	    /// `plan_overlays`' request JSON for `clips` (container ticks `from`/`to`, nil for none).
88	    static func request(
89	        _ clips: [UInt32], settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, module: String,
90	        schema: [String: Any], from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
91	    ) -> String {
92	        var args: [String: Any] = [
93	            "clips": clips.map { Int($0) }, "duration": settings.duration,
94	            "position": settings.position, "theme": settings.theme, "module": module,
95	            "schema": schema,
96	        ]
97	        if let from { args["from"] = from }
98	        if let to { args["to"] = to }
99	        let data =
100	            (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ["plan_overlays": args])) ?? Data()
101	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
102	    }
103	
104	    /// Asks the core for the plan over `clips` of `project` (the edited one, so inside a nest
105	    /// the nest's), one track per clip; throws the core's sentence as a `Refusal`.
106	    static func plan(
107	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor], project: ReelProject,
108	        settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, module: String, schema: [String: Any],
109	        from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
110	    ) throws -> ShortcutOverlayPlan {
111	        var ordered: [ReelCursor] = []
112	        for clip in clips {
113	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source, let track = tracks[id] else {
114	                throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "Clip \(clip.id)'s cursor file was not read.")
115	            }
116	            ordered.append(track)
117	        }
118	        let text: String
119	        do {
120	            text = try ReelCursor.query(
121	                request(
122	                    clips.map(\.id), settings: settings, module: module, schema: schema,
123	                    from: from, to: to),
124	                tracks: ordered, project: project)
125	        } catch {
126	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
127	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: AutoZoom.sentence(reason))
128	        }
129	        guard let answer = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))
130	            as? [String: Any]
131	        else { throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "The overlays' plan could not be read.") }
132	        let ops = try ((answer["ops"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []).map(op)
133	        func count(_ key: String) -> Int { (answer[key] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0 }
134	        return ShortcutOverlayPlan(
135	            ops: ops, added: count("added"), dropped: count("dropped"),
136	            merged: count("merged"),
137	            track: (answer["track"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0,
138	            newTrack: (answer["new_track"] as? Bool) ?? false,
139	            overlays: (answer["overlays"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? [])
140	    }
141	
142	    /// Both doors' run, on main, after the files are read: the module chosen by CU-81, the
143	    /// plan, and — only when the plan places something and no module could be reused — the
144	    /// template written into `graphics/` (not undoable, G-3) and the plan made again when the
145	    /// written name is not the one predicted.
146	    static func prepared(
147	        _ document: ProjectDocument, clips ids: [UInt32], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor],
148	        settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
149	    ) throws -> (plan: ShortcutOverlayPlan, module: String, written: Bool) {
150	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else {
151	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence + ".")
152	        }
153	        let template = try template()
154	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
155	        let clips = ids.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }
156	        func planned(_ module: String) throws -> ShortcutOverlayPlan {
157	            try plan(
158	                clips, tracks: tracks, project: document.editedProject, settings: settings,
159	                module: module, schema: template.schema, from: from, to: to)
160	        }
161	        if let reused = reusableModule(in: store, bytes: template.bytes) {
162	            return (try planned(reused), reused, false)
163	        }
164	        let predicted = store.uniqueModuleName(templateName)
165	        let first = try planned(predicted)
166	        guard first.added > 0 else { return (first, predicted, false) }
167	        let written: String
168	        do {
169	            written = try document.writeGraphicModule(from: template.url)
170	        } catch {
171	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
172	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: AutoZoom.sentence(reason))
173	        }
174	        guard written != predicted else { return (first, written, true) }
175	        return (try planned(written), written, true)
176	    }
177	
178	    /// One op of the answer, through `ReelOps.swift`'s factories.
179	    private static func op(_ o: [String: Any]) throws -> ReelOp {
180	        func ticks(_ key: String) -> Ticks { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value ?? 0 }
181	        switch o["op"] as? String {
182	        case "add_track":
183	            return .addTrack(
184	                index: (o["index"] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0, name: o["name"] as? String)
185	        case "add_graphic_clip":
186	            return .addGraphicClipRaw(
187	                track: (o["track"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0, at: ticks("at"),
188	                duration: ticks("duration"), name: (o["name"] as? String) ?? "",
189	                props: o["props"], schema: o["schema"])
190	        default:
191	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "The overlays' plan named an op it does not make.")
192	        }
193	    }
194	}

205	    /// The selected clips the menu offers overlays on, in id order; empty when any of them is

207	    private func shortcutOverlayClips(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
208	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
209	        let clips = document.selection.sorted().compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }
210	        guard clips.count == document.selection.count,
211	            AutoZoom.canOffer(clips, in: snapshot)

216	    @objc func addShortcutOverlays(_ sender: Any?) {
217	        guard let document, view.window?.attachedSheet == nil,
218	            !ShortcutOverlays.isPending(document)
219	        else {
220	            NSSound.beep()
221	            return
222	        }
223	        let ids = shortcutOverlayClips(document)
224	        guard !ids.isEmpty else {
225	            NSSound.beep()
226	            return
227	        }
228	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
229	        let files: [UInt32: URL]
230	        do {
231	            files = try AutoZoom.cursorFiles(ids.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, in: snapshot)
232	        } catch {
233	            showShortcutOverlayNotice(error.localizedDescription)
234	            return
235	        }
236	        let asked = document.project
237	        let scope = document.scope
238	        ShortcutOverlays.setPending(document, true)
239	        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async { [weak self] in
240	            let read = Result { try AutoZoom.readTracks(files) }
241	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
242	                ShortcutOverlays.setPending(document, false)
243	                self?.placeShortcutOverlays(document, ids, read, asked: asked, scope: scope)
244	            }
245	        }
246	    }

248	    /// The run's main half: refuse a changed project, place, and say what did not go as asked.
249	    private func placeShortcutOverlays(
250	        _ document: ProjectDocument, _ ids: [UInt32], _ read: Result<[UInt32: ReelCursor], Error>,
251	        asked: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?
252	    ) {
253	        let tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor]
254	        switch read {
255	        case .success(let value): tracks = value
256	        case .failure(let error):
257	            showShortcutOverlayNotice(error.localizedDescription)
258	            return
259	        }
260	        guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {
261	            showShortcutOverlayNotice(
262	                "The project changed while the cursor files were read, so no overlay was "
263	                    + "added. Choose Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays again.")
264	            return
265	        }
266	        do {
267	            let run = try ShortcutOverlays.prepared(
268	                document, clips: ids, tracks: tracks, settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings(),
269	                from: nil, to: nil)
270	            guard !run.plan.ops.isEmpty else {
271	                showShortcutOverlayNotice(ShortcutOverlays.nothingSentence)
272	                return
273	            }
274	            document.performGroupedEdit(ShortcutOverlays.actionName, run.plan.ops)
275	            if run.plan.dropped > 0 {
276	                showShortcutOverlayNotice(ShortcutOverlays.droppedSentence(run.plan.dropped))
277	            }
278	        } catch {
279	            showShortcutOverlayNotice(error.localizedDescription)
280	        }
281	    }

479	/// D_min(n) = 10n + 25 frames (CU-80): `keyboard-keys.js` presses its last
480	/// keycap at frame `pressAt + 5(n − 1)` = 10n + 9 (`pressAt` = 5n + 14) and
481	/// exits over the clip's last 15 frames, so the last press needs 16 frames
482	/// before the end.
483	pub(crate) fn min_frames(keycaps: usize) -> i64 {
484	    10 * keycaps as i64 + 25
485	}
486	
487	/// A chord's keycap count: its non-empty trimmed `+` tokens, the template's
488	/// own split.
489	fn keycaps(keys: &str) -> usize {
490	    keys.split('+').filter(|t| !t.trim().is_empty()).count()
491	}
492	
493	/// One press in container frames.
494	struct Press {
495	    frame: i64,
496	    keys: String,
497	}
498	
499	/// One overlay in container frames, `[start, end)`.
500	struct Overlay {
501	    start: i64,
502	    end: i64,
503	    keys: String,
504	    n: usize,
505	    count: u32,
506	}
507	
508	/// The overlays CU-80 makes of `presses` (in time order): the overlays,
509	/// the presses dropped and the presses merged.
510	fn lay_out(presses: &[Press], duration: i64, most_late: i64) -> (Vec<Overlay>, u32, u32) {
511	    let (mut out, mut dropped, mut merged): (Vec<Overlay>, u32, u32) = (Vec::new(), 0, 0);
512	    for p in presses {
513	        let n = keycaps(&p.keys);
514	        let length = duration.max(min_frames(n));
515	        let mut start = p.frame;
516	        if let Some(cur) = out.last_mut() {
517	            if p.frame < cur.end {
518	                if p.keys == cur.keys {
519	                    cur.end = cur.end.max(p.frame + duration);
520	                    cur.count += 1;
521	                    merged += 1;
522	                    continue;
523	                }
524	                start = p.frame.max(cur.start + min_frames(cur.n));
525	                if start - p.frame > most_late {
526	                    dropped += 1;
527	                    continue;
528	                }
529	                cur.end = start;
530	            }
531	        }
532	        out.push(Overlay {
533	            start,
534	            end: start + length,
535	            keys: p.keys.clone(),
536	            n,
537	            count: 1,
538	        });
539	    }
540	    (out, dropped, merged)
541	}

543	/// Checks every clip in CU-84's order.
544	fn check(project: &Project, clips: &[u32]) -> Result<(), String> {
545	    for (i, &id) in clips.iter().enumerate() {
546	        if clips[..i].contains(&id) {
547	            return Err(format!("clip {id} is named twice"));
548	        }
549	        let clip = project.require_clip(id)?;
550	        let Source::Media {
551	            media, reversed, ..
552	        } = &clip.source
553	        else {
554	            return Err(format!("clip {id} is not a media clip"));
555	        };
556	        if project
557	            .media(*media)
558	            .and_then(|m| m.cursor.as_ref())
559	            .is_none()
560	        {
561	            return Err(format!("clip {id}'s media {media} has no cursor file"));
562	        }
563	        if *reversed {
564	            return Err(format!(
565	                "clip {id} plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play \
566	                 forward"
567	            ));
568	        }
569	    }
570	    Ok(())
571	}

573	/// The track CU-83 picks for the span `[from, to)`: the id and whether it
574	/// is new.
575	fn track_for(project: &Project, clips: &[u32], span: (Ticks, Ticks)) -> (u32, bool) {
576	    let index_of = |track: u32| project.tracks.iter().position(|t| t.id == track);
577	    let front_of_clips = clips
578	        .iter()
579	        .filter_map(|&id| project.clip(id))
580	        .filter_map(|c| index_of(c.track))
581	        .max()
582	        .unwrap_or(0);
583	    let found = project
584	        .tracks
585	        .iter()
586	        .enumerate()
587	        .rev()
588	        .find(|(_, t)| t.name == TRACK_NAME);
589	    if let Some((index, track)) = found {
590	        let free = !project.clips.iter().any(|c| {
591	            c.track == track.id && c.start < span.1 && span.0 < c.start.saturating_add(c.duration)
592	        });
593	        if index > front_of_clips && !track.locked && !track.hidden && track.matte.is_none() && free
594	        {
595	            return (track.id, false);
596	        }
597	    }
598	    (project.next_id, true)
599	}

601	/// Answers `plan_overlays` (CU-80…CU-84) against `tracks`, one per clip.
602	pub(crate) fn plan_overlays(
603	    tracks: &[&CursorTrack],
604	    project: &Project,
605	    args: PlanOverlaysArgs,
606	) -> Result<Value, String> {
607	    let (lo, hi) = DURATION_RANGE;
608	    if !(args.duration.is_finite() && (lo..=hi).contains(&args.duration)) {
609	        return Err(format!(
610	            "duration is {} s; it runs {lo}–{hi}",
611	            args.duration
612	        ));
613	    }
614	    if let (Some(from), Some(to)) = (args.from, args.to) {
615	        if to <= from {
616	            return Err(format!("to ({to}) must be after from ({from})"));
617	        }
618	    }
619	    if args.clips.is_empty() {
620	        return Err("plan_overlays needs at least one clip".into());
621	    }
622	    if tracks.len() != args.clips.len() {
623	        return Err(format!(
624	            "plan_overlays reads one cursor track per clip; {} clips and {} tracks were given",
625	            args.clips.len(),
626	            tracks.len()
627	        ));
628	    }
629	    check(project, &args.clips)?;
630	    let fps = project.canvas.fps;
631	    let frame = project.frame();
632	    let index = |t: Ticks| time::frame_index(t, fps).unwrap_or(t / frame);
633	    let tick = |i: i64| time::tick_at_frame(i, fps).unwrap_or(i * frame);
634	    let window = (
635	        args.from.unwrap_or(Ticks::MIN),
636	        args.to.unwrap_or(Ticks::MAX),
637	    );
638	    let mut presses: Vec<Press> = Vec::new();
639	    for (i, &id) in args.clips.iter().enumerate() {
640	        let clip = project.require_clip(id)?;
641	        let Some((_, source_in)) = media_in(clip) else {
642	            continue;
643	        };
644	        let length = project.content_length_in_source(clip);
645	        let k = &tracks[i].file().keys.shortcut;
646	        for j in 0..k.t.len() {
647	            let s = us_to_ticks(k.t[j]);
648	            if s < source_in || s >= source_in.saturating_add(length) {
649	                continue;
650	            }
651	            let at = clip.start.saturating_add(clip_time(clip, s - source_in));
652	            if at < window.0 || at >= window.1 {
653	                continue;
654	            }
655	            presses.push(Press {
656	                frame: index(project.snapped(at)),
657	                keys: k.keys[j].clone(),
658	            });
659	        }
660	    }
661	    // Stable: equal frames keep the given clip order.
662	    presses.sort_by_key(|p| p.frame);
663	    let duration = index(seconds_to_ticks(args.duration));
664	    let most_late = index(seconds_to_ticks(MOST_LATE));
665	    let (overlays, dropped, merged) = lay_out(&presses, duration, most_late);
666	    let (Some(first), Some(last)) = (overlays.first(), overlays.last()) else {
667	        return Ok(json!({
668	            "ops": [], "added": 0, "dropped": dropped, "merged": merged,
669	            "track": null, "new_track": false, "overlays": [],
670	        }));
671	    };
672	    let span = (tick(first.start), tick(last.end));
673	    let (track, new_track) = track_for(project, &args.clips, span);
674	    let mut ops: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
675	    if new_track {
676	        ops.push(json!({"op": "add_track", "index": project.tracks.len(), "name": TRACK_NAME}));
677	    }
678	    let mut answered: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
679	    for o in &overlays {
680	        let at = tick(o.start);
681	        let length = tick(o.end) - at;
682	        let label = if o.count > 1 {
683	            format!("×{}", o.count)
684	        } else {
685	            String::new()
686	        };
687	        let mut op = json!({
688	            "op": "add_graphic_clip", "track": track, "at": at, "duration": length,
689	            "name": args.module,
690	            "props": {"keys": o.keys, "label": label, "position": args.position.name(),
691	                      "theme": args.theme.name()},
692	        });
693	        if let Some(schema) = &args.schema {
694	            op["schema"] = schema.clone();
695	        }
696	        ops.push(op);
697	        answered.push(json!({"at": at, "duration": length, "keys": o.keys, "label": label}));
698	    }
699	    Ok(json!({
700	        "ops": ops, "added": overlays.len(), "dropped": dropped, "merged": merged,
701	        "track": track, "new_track": new_track, "overlays": answered,
702	    }))
703	}
704	//! Bursts of input in a cursor file (spec §11 CU-25, CU-70): the typing
705	//! stretches an `events` request answers and Auto Zoom anchors on, and the
706	//! scroll bursts that end an Auto Zoom visit, by CU7's figures. CU9b reads
707	//! the same stretches. Both are one run finder with their own figures.
708	
709	/// Marks closer than this belong to one stretch (strictly under 1.0 s).
710	pub const TYPING_GAP_US: i64 = 1_000_000;
711	/// The fewest marks a stretch holds.
712	pub const TYPING_MIN_MARKS: usize = 3;
713	/// Wheel events closer than this belong to one burst (strictly under 1.0 s).
714	pub const SCROLL_GAP_US: i64 = 1_000_000;
715	/// The fewest wheel events a burst holds.
716	pub const SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS: usize = 3;
717	
718	/// Each run of `t` (µs, in order) whose neighbours are less than `gap`
719	/// apart and which holds at least `min` entries, as (first, last, count).
720	fn runs(t: &[i64], gap: i64, min: usize) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
721	    let mut out = Vec::new();
722	    let mut start = 0;
723	    for i in 1..=t.len() {
724	        if i == t.len() || t[i] - t[i - 1] >= gap {
725	            if i - start >= min {
726	                out.push((t[start], t[i - 1], i - start));
727	            }
728	            start = i;
729	        }
730	    }
731	    out
732	}
733	
734	/// The typing stretches of `t` (the `typed` marks' µs, in order): each run
735	/// of marks less than `TYPING_GAP_US` apart holding at least
736	/// `TYPING_MIN_MARKS`, as (first mark, last mark, marks).
737	pub(crate) fn typing_stretches(t: &[i64]) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
738	    runs(t, TYPING_GAP_US, TYPING_MIN_MARKS)
739	}
740	
741	/// The scroll bursts of `t` (the `scrolls`' µs, in order): each run of
742	/// wheel events less than `SCROLL_GAP_US` apart holding at least
743	/// `SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS`, as (first, last, events).
744	pub(crate) fn scroll_bursts(t: &[i64]) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
745	    runs(t, SCROLL_GAP_US, SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS)
746	}
747	//! Auto Zoom's visits (spec §11 CU-70): anchors in container time become
748	//! visits, and visits become planned zoom-ins, pans, follow pans and zoom
749	//! backs, still in container time and not yet on any clip. Pure: no
750	//! `Project`, no cursor file — `cursor_zoom.rs` maps the file into
751	//! [`Anchor`]s, scroll-burst starts, barriers and a cursor sampler, and
752	//! moves what comes back onto clips (CU-74).
753	//!
754	//! Positions are in P: source pixels from the centre of the UNCROPPED
755	//! picture, y down. A region is centred on its aim and clamped inside the
756	//! cropped rect ([`Frame`]); `cursor_zoom.rs` turns P into Q per clip.
757	//!
758	//! **Barriers** are cuts a hold may not cross (a cut into a clip that was
759	//! not given, or into one whose kept action meets the hold) and the run's
760	//! end. No visit spans one; a visit whose zoom back would end past one is
761	//! closed with a zoom back ending at it, counted when the barrier is a cut.
762

765	/// A zoom back's length: 0.8 s.
766	pub(crate) const BACK: Ticks = TIMESCALE * 8 / 10;
767	/// A follow pan's length: 0.5 s.
768	const FOLLOW_PAN: Ticks = TIMESCALE / 2;
769	/// How long the cursor stays outside the inner 70 % before a follow pan.
770	const FOLLOW_OUTSIDE: Ticks = TIMESCALE * 3 / 10;
771	/// At most one follow pan a second, start to start.
772	const FOLLOW_EVERY: Ticks = TIMESCALE;
773	/// The follow sampler's step: 10 Hz.
774	const SAMPLE: Ticks = TIMESCALE / 10;
775	/// A zoom back ending under this before the next zoom-in starts merges.
776	const MERGE_GAP: Ticks = TIMESCALE;
777	/// Half the inner part an anchor must leave to pan: 60 %.
778	const ANCHOR_HALF: f64 = 0.3;
779	/// Half the inner part the followed cursor must leave: 70 %.
780	const FOLLOW_HALF: f64 = 0.35;

793	/// The region's size and the cropped rect it is clamped inside, in P.
794	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
795	pub(crate) struct Frame {
796	    pub size: (f64, f64),
797	    pub min: (f64, f64),
798	    pub max: (f64, f64),
799	}
800	
801	impl Frame {
802	    /// The region centre for an aim: clamped so the region stays inside
803	    /// the cropped rect, centred on an axis it exceeds.
804	    pub(crate) fn clamp(&self, p: (f64, f64)) -> (f64, f64) {
805	        let axis = |v: f64, size: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64| {
806	            if size >= hi - lo {
807	                (lo + hi) / 2.0
808	            } else {
809	                v.clamp(lo + size / 2.0, hi - size / 2.0)
810	            }
811	        };
812	        (
813	            axis(p.0, self.size.0, self.min.0, self.max.0),
814	            axis(p.1, self.size.1, self.min.1, self.max.1),
815	        )
816	    }
817	
818	    fn outside(&self, centre: (f64, f64), p: (f64, f64), half: f64) -> bool {
819	        (p.0 - centre.0).abs() > half * self.size.0 || (p.1 - centre.1).abs() > half * self.size.1
820	    }
821	}

880	struct Visit {
881	    anchors: Vec<Anchor>,
882	    last: Ticks,
883	    back: Ticks,
884	}
885	
886	/// Anchors (any order), scroll-burst starts, barriers, the figures and the
887	/// frame, and the cursor in P at a container time → the run's plan.
888	pub(crate) fn plan(
889	    mut anchors: Vec<Anchor>,
890	    bursts: &[Ticks],
891	    barriers: &[Barrier],
892	    timing: Timing,
893	    frame: Frame,
894	    cursor: &dyn Fn(Ticks) -> Option<(f64, f64)>,
895	) -> Plan {
896	    anchors.sort_by_key(|a| a.t);
897	    let barrier_in = |lo: Ticks, hi: Ticks| barriers.iter().any(|b| lo < b.at && b.at <= hi);
898	    let mut visits: Vec<Visit> = Vec::new();
899	    for a in anchors {
900	        let joins = visits.last().is_some_and(|v| {
901	            let prev = v.anchors.last().map_or(a.t, |p| p.t);
902	            a.t <= v.last + timing.stay
903	                && !bursts.iter().any(|&b| v.last < b && b < a.t)
904	                && !barrier_in(prev, a.t)
905	        });
906	        match visits.last_mut() {
907	            Some(v) if joins => {
908	                v.last = v.last.max(a.end);
909	                v.anchors.push(a);
910	            }
911	            _ => visits.push(Visit {
912	                anchors: vec![a],
913	                last: a.end,
914	                back: 0,
915	            }),
916	        }
917	    }
918	    let mut out = Plan {
919	        visits: visits.len(),
920	        ..Plan::default()
921	    };
922	    // Each visit's zoom back: Stay after its last activity, or the first
923	    // scroll burst after its last anchor, closed at the next barrier.
924	    let mut closed_by = vec![false; visits.len()];
925	    for (i, v) in visits.iter_mut().enumerate() {
926	        let last_anchor = v.anchors.last().map_or(0, |a| a.t);
927	        let mut back = v.last + timing.stay;
928	        if let Some(&b) = bursts.iter().find(|&&b| b > last_anchor) {
929	            back = back.min(b);
930	        }
931	        if let Some(bar) = barriers.iter().find(|b| b.at > last_anchor) {
932	            if back + BACK > bar.at {
933	                back = bar.at - BACK;
934	                closed_by[i] = true;
935	                if bar.counted {
936	                    out.closed += 1;
937	                }
938	            }
939	        }
940	        v.back = back;
941	    }
942	    // Chains: a visit whose zoom back would end under MERGE_GAP before the
943	    // next one's zoom-in starts runs on into it with one pan.
944	    let mut chains: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
945	    for i in 0..visits.len() {
946	        let merge = i > 0 && !closed_by[i - 1] && {
947	            let (v, w) = (&visits[i - 1], &visits[i]);
948	            let next = w.anchors[0].t;
949	            let prev = v.anchors.last().map_or(next, |a| a.t);
950	            next - timing.lead - (v.back + BACK) < MERGE_GAP && !barrier_in(prev, next)
951	        };
952	        match chains.last_mut() {
953	            Some(chain) if merge => chain.push(i),
954	            _ => chains.push(vec![i]),
955	        }
956	    }
957	    for chain in chains {
958	        plan_chain(&chain, &visits, timing, frame, cursor, &mut out);
959	    }
960	    out
961	}

963	/// One hold: a zoom-in, the anchors' pans (a merged visit's first anchor
964	/// always pans), follow pans, a zoom back.
965	fn plan_chain(
966	    chain: &[usize],
967	    visits: &[Visit],
968	    timing: Timing,
969	    frame: Frame,
970	    cursor: &dyn Fn(Ticks) -> Option<(f64, f64)>,
971	    out: &mut Plan,
972	) {
973	    let mut anchors: Vec<(Anchor, bool)> = Vec::new();
974	    for (k, &i) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
975	        for (j, a) in visits[i].anchors.iter().enumerate() {
976	            anchors.push((*a, k > 0 && j == 0));
977	        }
978	    }
979	    let back = visits[chain[chain.len() - 1]].back;
980	    let first = anchors[0].0;
981	    let mut region = frame.clamp(first.p);
982	    let hold_start = first.t - timing.lead;
983	    out.actions.push(Planned {
984	        from: hold_start,
985	        to: first.t,
986	        kind: Kind::In,
987	        aim: Some(region),
988	    });
989	    let mut busy = first.t;
990	    let mut next = 1;
991	    let mut t = first.t;
992	    let mut outside_since: Option<Ticks> = None;
993	    let mut last_follow: Option<Ticks> = None;
994	    loop {
995	        while next < anchors.len() && anchors[next].0.t - timing.lead <= t {
996	            let (a, forced) = anchors[next];
997	            if forced || frame.outside(region, a.p, ANCHOR_HALF) {
998	                let start = (a.t - timing.lead).max(busy);
999	                if a.t - start >= timing.frame {
1000	                    region = frame.clamp(a.p);
1001	                    out.actions.push(Planned {
1002	                        from: start,
1003	                        to: a.t,
1004	                        kind: Kind::Pan,
1005	                        aim: Some(region),
1006	                    });
1007	                    busy = a.t;
1008	                }
1009	            }
1010	            outside_since = None;
1011	            next += 1;
1012	        }
1013	        if t >= back {
1014	            break;
1015	        }
1016	        let watched = timing.follow && t >= busy;
1017	        match watched.then(|| cursor(t)).flatten() {
1018	            Some(p) if frame.outside(region, p, FOLLOW_HALF) => {
1019	                let since = *outside_since.get_or_insert(t);
1020	                let end = t + FOLLOW_PAN;
1021	                let free = !anchors[next..]
1022	                    .iter()
1023	                    .any(|(a, _)| a.t - timing.lead < end && t < a.t);
1024	                if t - since >= FOLLOW_OUTSIDE
1025	                    && last_follow.is_none_or(|l| t - l >= FOLLOW_EVERY)
1026	                    && end <= back
1027	                    && free
1028	                {
1029	                    region = frame.clamp(p);
1030	                    out.actions.push(Planned {
1031	                        from: t,
1032	                        to: end,
1033	                        kind: Kind::Follow,
1034	                        aim: Some(region),
1035	                    });
1036	                    busy = end;
1037	                    last_follow = Some(t);
1038	                    outside_since = None;
1039	                }
1040	            }
1041	            _ => outside_since = None,
1042	        }
1043	        t += SAMPLE;
1044	    }
1045	    let from = back.max(busy);
1046	    let to = back + BACK;
1047	    if to - from >= timing.frame {
1048	        out.actions.push(Planned {
1049	            from,
1050	            to,
1051	            kind: Kind::Back,
1052	            aim: None,
1053	        });
1054	    }
1055	    out.holds.push((hold_start, to));
1056	}

2	**What a recording lands with.** With **Cursor** set to **Separate**, macOS draws no pointer into the movie, the cursor file says the pointer is not in the picture, and the landed clip gets a **Cursor** section, with the pointer drawn as recorded. With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording (in a new project whose only other change is that, the undo name is "Cursor Clicks"). Nothing else is set: **Polish** is one click away. With **In the picture**, the pointer is in the movie, its cursor file says so, and the clip shows no **Cursor** section, so nothing is drawn twice.

4	### Shortcuts and Input Monitoring
5	
6	With **Record shortcuts** ticked, a display or window recording also writes your keyboard into each stretch's cursor file, in two kinds:
7	
8	- **A shortcut**, with its keys spelled out, for example `cmd+shift+4`. A key you press while holding ⌘ or ⌃ is a shortcut, and so is ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc. ⇧ on its own never makes one, and neither does ⌥ with any other key (⌥E types é). The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the key: a named key (`return`, `tab`, `space`, `left`, `f5` and so on) or the character the key types with no modifier, lowercased (`+` is spelled `plus`).
9	- **A typing mark**: the time of every other key you press, and of every key held down until it repeats. A typing mark never says which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all.
10	
11	**Nothing is recorded while any app holds secure input**, as a password field does: not a shortcut, not even a typing mark. A password field that doesn't turn secure input on, such as a Terminal `sudo` prompt with **Secure Keyboard Entry** off, is recorded as typing marks only, with no characters. Keys pressed while the recording is paused aren't recorded.
12	
13	Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission (see [Permissions](#permissions)). While it records, the menu-bar item shows the keyboard mark (see [The menu-bar item](#the-menu-bar-item)). *Agents:* `record_screen` with `keys: "shortcuts"`, and `get_cursor_events` reads the shortcuts and typing back.

15	## Auto Zoom
16	
17	**Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** zooms a screen recording in where things happen, from its cursor file: it arrives just before each click, stays while you keep working there, and zooms back out once you stop. Every zoom it makes is an ordinary action, like one from [Zoom to Region](motion-and-transitions.md#zoom-to-a-region), so you can move, retime, change or delete any of them afterwards. The whole plan is one undo step, "Auto Zoom".
18	
19	Select one or more clips whose movies have cursor files (see [The cursor](#the-cursor)) and choose the item. It works inside an open nest too. It is greyed when a selected clip is not a movie with a cursor file.
20	
21	| Control | What it does | Default |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| **Zoom** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× (1.25–4) |
24	| **Arrive** | How many seconds before a click the zoom-in starts. | 0.6 s (0.2–2) |
25	| **Stay** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it zooms back out. | 2.5 s (0.5–10) |
26	| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | on |
27	| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing too, aimed at the last click before them. Greyed when the recording holds no typing (see [Shortcuts and Input Monitoring](#shortcuts-and-input-monitoring)). | on when there is typing |
28	| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Off keeps your own zooms. | off |
29	| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % [motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur) (a 180° shutter), so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. A clip that already has a Motion Blur keeps its own. | on |
30	
31	The sheet reads the cursor files first ("Reading cursor files…"), then says what Zoom would do, for example "5 zooms in 2 visits." and, when some planned zooms meet an action already on the clip, "1 dropped where an action is already set." It says so instead when a clip can't be planned. Frame Job remembers Zoom, Arrive, Stay, Follow, Replace and Motion blur for next time, but only once you change one; Zoom on typing is never remembered.
32	
33	How it plans:
34	
35	- **A visit** starts at a click (any button) or a stretch of typing. A later click within **Stay** of the last activity joins it; a longer gap, or scrolling, ends it. A visit is a zoom-in that arrives **Arrive** seconds before its first click, a pan to each later click that falls outside the middle 60 % of the view, and a 0.8 s zoom back out. When one visit would zoom out less than a second before the next zooms in, it pans across instead.
36	- **Follow** adds a half-second pan when the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the view for 0.3 s, at most one a second.
37	- **The view** keeps the canvas's shape and never shows past the edge of the picture: near a corner it stops at the corner.
38	- **Split clips.** The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording, and every zoom out goes back to the first half's placement. No zoom crosses a cut. A zoom held across a cut carries into the next half, which starts already zoomed; when that half has an action of its own there, or wasn't selected, the zoom goes back out at the cut instead.
39	- **Your own actions.** A planned zoom that would overlap an action already on the clip is left out. With **Replace existing zooms**, the clips' existing zooms are removed first — only zooms, never a speed change, a fade or anything else.
40	
41	A clip placed smaller than the canvas (side by side with a camera, or a picture in picture) is refused: "Clip C is placed smaller than the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto Zoom inside the nest." Nest it, open the nest and run Auto Zoom there; the zooms then fill the nest. A clip that plays reversed is refused too.
42	
43	*Agents:* `auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments; its `motion_blur` (0–1, 0.5 by default) is the sheet's Motion blur, and its answer's `blurred` counts the clips it gave one.

45	## Shortcut overlays
46	
47	**Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** shows each keyboard shortcut you pressed while recording as keycaps on screen, at the moment you pressed it. It needs a recording made with **Record shortcuts** on (see [Shortcuts and Input Monitoring](#shortcuts-and-input-monitoring)); only shortcuts are recorded, never what you typed.
48	
49	Select one or more clips whose movies have cursor files and choose the item. There is no sheet: it reads the cursor files and places one **Keyboard keys** graphic clip per shortcut, at the bottom of the picture in the dark theme, each shown for 1.5 s. The whole change is one undo step, "Add Shortcut Overlays". It works inside an open nest too, and is greyed when a selected clip is not a movie with a cursor file.
50	
51	- **Where they go.** On the front-most track named "Shortcuts" when it is in front of the clips, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free where the overlays go; otherwise on a new "Shortcuts" track at the front.
52	- **How long.** Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out: (10 × keys + 25) frames, so 1.5 s for a two-key shortcut at 30 fps.
53	- **Repeats.** Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends keeps it up 1.5 s past the last press, labelled "×2", "×3" and so on.
54	- **Shortcuts close together.** A different shortcut pressed while one is showing takes over once the first has had its minimum. When that would show it more than half a second late, it is left out, and a sheet says how many were: "1 shortcut came too close to show."
55	- **The graphic.** The overlays are drawn by the project's copy of the bundled Keyboard keys template, written into the project's graphics the first time and reused after; if you have edited that copy, a fresh one is written beside it. Change a clip's look in its Graphic sub-tab like any graphic.
56	
57	When no shortcut was recorded in the selected clips, a sheet says "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added." A clip that plays reversed is refused.
58	
59	*Agents:* `add_shortcut_overlays` places the same overlays, and takes `duration`, `position` (bottom, center, top), `theme` (dark, light) and a `from`/`to` range.
60	
61	## Speeding up typing
62	
63	**Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer does not sit through every keystroke. It reads the typing from the recording's cursor file: a run of at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. Only the moments are recorded, never which keys.
64	
65	Select one or more clips whose movies have cursor files and choose the item. The sheet has three settings, remembered for next time:
66	
67	| Setting | Default | What it does |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| Rate | ×4 (×2 to ×8) | How much faster the typing plays |
70	| Shortest stretch | 3 s (1 to 30 s) | Typing shorter than this is left alone |
71	| Keep pitch | On | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch (off, it rises like a fast tape) |
72	
73	The sheet says what Apply would do, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s.", or "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." Apply makes one undo step, "Speed Up Typing". It works inside an open nest too, and is greyed when a selected clip is not a movie with a cursor file.
74	
75	- **Speech stays at normal speed.** Any part of a stretch where a clip with sound under it has speech, on any track, is left at normal speed. Frame Job finds the speech on this Mac (the same detection Duck by Speech uses) and saves it with the project in the same undo step. While it is still being detected the sheet says "Waiting for speech detection on …" and updates by itself; after five minutes it stops waiting and asks you to close the sheet and try again. On a Mac where speech detection cannot run, it says so and changes nothing.
76	- **Shortcuts stay at normal speed.** A recorded shortcut and the overlay that shows it (its clip on a "Shortcuts" track, or 1.5 s when there is none) are never sped up, so add the overlays first.
77	- **Clean edges.** Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends.
78	- **Split recordings.** The halves of a recording you split are treated as one: typing across the cut is one stretch.
79	- **Everything stays in step.** Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](speed.md#retime-a-range) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync and everything after moves up. The sound in a sped stretch is sped too.
80	
81	Nothing changes when any stretch cannot be sped (a locked track after it, a transition touching it, a detached pair in it…): the sheet names the stretch and the reason. A clip that plays reversed is refused. Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks first, as [The ×12 question](speed.md#the-12-question) says.
82	
83	*Agents:* `speed_up_typing` does the same, and takes `rate`, `shortest`, `keep_pitch` and a `from`/`to` range. It answers each sped range and the time saved.

102	/// CU-118 (c)): the owner's 50 % by default, 0 for none.
103	struct AutoZoomSettings: Equatable {
104	    var zoom = 2.0, lead = 0.6, stay = 2.5
105	    var follow = true, typing = true, replace = false
106	    var motionBlur = 0.5
107	
108	    static let zoomRange: ClosedRange<Double> = 1.25...4
109	    static let leadRange: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.2...2.0
110	    static let stayRange: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.5...10.0
111	
112	    static let zoomKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomZoom"
113	    static let leadKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomLead"
114	    static let stayKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomStay"
115	    static let followKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomFollow"
116	    static let replaceKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomReplace"
117	    /// The sheet's "Motion blur" checkbox, remembered as a Bool: on is `motionBlurShutter`, off 0.
118	    static let motionBlurKey = "FrameJobAutoZoomMotionBlur"
119	    /// The shutter "Motion blur" sets when on (the owner's answer, 2026-11-01: a 180° shutter).
120	    static let motionBlurShutter = 0.5

122	    /// The remembered values, each clamped into its range; the default for a key not stored.
123	    /// Read through `double(forKey:)` and `bool(forKey:)`, so a launch argument's string
124	    /// (`-FrameJobAutoZoomLead 1`) reads as its number.
125	    static func remembered(_ d: UserDefaults) -> AutoZoomSettings {
126	        var s = AutoZoomSettings()
127	        func number(_ key: String, _ range: ClosedRange<Double>, _ value: inout Double) {
128	            guard d.object(forKey: key) != nil else { return }
129	            let v = d.double(forKey: key)
130	            if v.isFinite, v > 0 { value = min(max(v, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound) }
131	        }
132	        number(zoomKey, zoomRange, &s.zoom)
133	        number(leadKey, leadRange, &s.lead)
134	        number(stayKey, stayRange, &s.stay)
135	        if d.object(forKey: followKey) != nil { s.follow = d.bool(forKey: followKey) }
136	        if d.object(forKey: replaceKey) != nil { s.replace = d.bool(forKey: replaceKey) }
137	        if d.object(forKey: motionBlurKey) != nil {
138	            s.motionBlur = d.bool(forKey: motionBlurKey) ? motionBlurShutter : 0
139	        }
140	        return s

145	    func remember(changedFrom opened: AutoZoomSettings, in d: UserDefaults) {
146	        if zoom != opened.zoom { d.set(zoom, forKey: Self.zoomKey) }
147	        if lead != opened.lead { d.set(lead, forKey: Self.leadKey) }

279	        else { throw Refusal(message: "Auto Zoom's plan could not be read.") }
280	        var ops = try ((answer["ops"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []).map(op)
281	        func count(_ key: String) -> Int { (answer[key] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0 }
282	        let actions = (answer["actions"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []
283	        let blurred = unblurred(actions, in: project.snapshot)
284	        if settings.motionBlur > 0, !blurred.isEmpty {
285	            ops.append(
286	                .setVideo(clips: blurred, patch: VideoPatch(motionBlur: settings.motionBlur)))
287	        }
288	        return AutoZoomPlan(
289	            ops: ops, visits: count("visits"), added: count("added"),
290	            replaced: count("replaced"), dropped: count("dropped"),
291	            closedAtCut: count("closed_at_cut"), basesSet: count("bases_set"),
292	            actions: actions, blurred: settings.motionBlur > 0 ? blurred.count : 0)
293	    }
294	
295	    /// The distinct clips the planned actions name, in first-named order, whose BASE
296	    /// `video.motion_blur` is 0 (CU-118 (c)): a clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
297	    private static func unblurred(_ actions: [[String: Any]], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
298	        -> [UInt32]
299	    {
300	        var clips: [UInt32] = []
301	        for action in actions {
302	            guard let id = (action["clip"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value, !clips.contains(id),
303	                let clip = snapshot.clip(id), (clip.video?.motionBlur ?? 0) <= 0
304	            else { continue }
305	            clips.append(id)
306	        }
307	        return clips
308	    }
309	
310	    /// The core's lowercase sentence as one a person reads: capitalised, with a full stop.
311	    static func sentence(_ core: String) -> String {
312	        guard let first = core.first else { return core }
313	        let text = first.uppercased() + core.dropFirst()
314	        return text.hasSuffix(".") ? text : text + "."
315	    }
316	
317	    /// One op of the answer, through `ReelOps.swift`'s factories.
318	    private static func op(_ o: [String: Any]) throws -> ReelOp {
319	        func id(_ key: String) -> UInt32 { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0 }
320	        func ticks(_ key: String) -> Ticks { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value ?? 0 }
321	        switch o["op"] as? String {
322	        case "remove_action":
323	            return .removeAction(clip: id("clip"), action: id("action"))
324	        case "set_video":
325	            let clips = ((o["clips"] as? [NSNumber]) ?? []).map(\.uint32Value)
326	            return .setVideoRaw(clips: clips, patch: o["patch"] ?? [String: Any]())
327	        case "add_zoom_action":
328	            return .addZoomActionRaw(
329	                clip: id("clip"), at: ticks("at"), duration: ticks("duration"),
330	                region: o["region"] ?? NSNull(),
331	                fit: (o["fit"] as? String).flatMap(ZoomFit.init(rawValue:)),
332	                curve: (o["curve"] as? String).flatMap(Curve.init(rawValue:)))
333	        default:
334	            throw Refusal(message: "Auto Zoom's plan named an op it does not make.")
335	        }
336	    }
337	}

11	/// What a run places with (CU-80's defaults; the owner's answer: bottom, dark). Nothing is
12	/// remembered: the menu item has no sheet to change it.
13	struct ShortcutOverlaySettings: Equatable {

15	    var position = "bottom"
16	    var theme = "dark"

24	struct ShortcutOverlayPlan {
25	    let ops: [ReelOp]
26	    let added, dropped, merged: Int
27	    let track: UInt32
28	    let newTrack: Bool

33	    /// The undo step's name, both doors.
34	    static let actionName = "Add Shortcut Overlays"
35	    /// The bundled template the overlays are drawn by.
36	    static let templateName = "keyboard-keys"

40	        "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added."

43	    static func droppedSentence(_ n: Int) -> String {
44	        n == 1
45	            ? "1 shortcut came too close to show."
46	            : "\(n) shortcuts came too close to show."

50	    private static var pending: Set<ObjectIdentifier> = []

52	    static func isPending(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
53	        pending.contains(ObjectIdentifier(document))
54	    }

64	    /// The bundled `keyboard-keys.js`: its URL, its bytes and the schema
65	    /// `GraphicTemplateLibrary` compiled from it. Main (the library's first read).
66	    static func template() throws -> (url: URL, bytes: Data, schema: [String: Any]) {
67	        guard let found = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: templateName) else {
68	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(
69	                message: "The bundled \(templateName) template is missing from this build.")
70	        }
71	        guard case .compiled(_, _, _, let schema) = found.entry,
72	            let bytes = try? Data(contentsOf: found.template.url)
73	        else {
74	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(
75	                message: "The bundled \(templateName) template does not compile.")
76	        }
77	        return (found.template.url, bytes, schema)
78	    }

80	    /// CU-81: a module of `store` whose bytes equal the template's — `keyboard-keys` first,
81	    /// else the lowest name — or nil.
82	    static func reusableModule(in store: GraphicStore, bytes: Data) -> String? {
83	        let same = store.scan.modules.values.filter { $0.bytes == bytes }.map(\.name)
84	        return same.contains(templateName) ? templateName : same.min()
85	    }

88	    static func request(
89	        _ clips: [UInt32], settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, module: String,
90	        schema: [String: Any], from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
91	    ) -> String {
92	        var args: [String: Any] = [
93	            "clips": clips.map { Int($0) }, "duration": settings.duration,
94	            "position": settings.position, "theme": settings.theme, "module": module,
95	            "schema": schema,
96	        ]
97	        if let from { args["from"] = from }
98	        if let to { args["to"] = to }
99	        let data =
100	            (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ["plan_overlays": args])) ?? Data()
101	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)

104	    /// Asks the core for the plan over `clips` of `project` (the edited one, so inside a nest
105	    /// the nest's), one track per clip; throws the core's sentence as a `Refusal`.
106	    static func plan(
107	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor], project: ReelProject,
108	        settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, module: String, schema: [String: Any],
109	        from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
110	    ) throws -> ShortcutOverlayPlan {
111	        var ordered: [ReelCursor] = []
112	        for clip in clips {
113	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source, let track = tracks[id] else {
114	                throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "Clip \(clip.id)'s cursor file was not read.")
115	            }
116	            ordered.append(track)
117	        }
118	        let text: String
119	        do {
120	            text = try ReelCursor.query(
121	                request(
122	                    clips.map(\.id), settings: settings, module: module, schema: schema,
123	                    from: from, to: to),
124	                tracks: ordered, project: project)
125	        } catch {
126	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
127	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: AutoZoom.sentence(reason))
128	        }
129	        guard let answer = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))
130	            as? [String: Any]
131	        else { throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "The overlays' plan could not be read.") }
132	        let ops = try ((answer["ops"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []).map(op)
133	        func count(_ key: String) -> Int { (answer[key] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0 }
134	        return ShortcutOverlayPlan(
135	            ops: ops, added: count("added"), dropped: count("dropped"),
136	            merged: count("merged"),
137	            track: (answer["track"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0,
138	            newTrack: (answer["new_track"] as? Bool) ?? false,
139	            overlays: (answer["overlays"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? [])
140	    }
141	
142	    /// Both doors' run, on main, after the files are read: the module chosen by CU-81, the
143	    /// plan, and — only when the plan places something and no module could be reused — the
144	    /// template written into `graphics/` (not undoable, G-3) and the plan made again when the
145	    /// written name is not the one predicted.
146	    static func prepared(
147	        _ document: ProjectDocument, clips ids: [UInt32], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor],
148	        settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings, from: Ticks?, to: Ticks?
149	    ) throws -> (plan: ShortcutOverlayPlan, module: String, written: Bool) {
150	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else {
151	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence + ".")
152	        }
153	        let template = try template()
154	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
155	        let clips = ids.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }
156	        func planned(_ module: String) throws -> ShortcutOverlayPlan {
157	            try plan(
158	                clips, tracks: tracks, project: document.editedProject, settings: settings,
159	                module: module, schema: template.schema, from: from, to: to)
160	        }
161	        if let reused = reusableModule(in: store, bytes: template.bytes) {
162	            return (try planned(reused), reused, false)
163	        }
164	        let predicted = store.uniqueModuleName(templateName)
165	        let first = try planned(predicted)
166	        guard first.added > 0 else { return (first, predicted, false) }
167	        let written: String
168	        do {
169	            written = try document.writeGraphicModule(from: template.url)
170	        } catch {
171	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
172	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: AutoZoom.sentence(reason))
173	        }
174	        guard written != predicted else { return (first, written, true) }
175	        return (try planned(written), written, true)
176	    }
177	
178	    /// One op of the answer, through `ReelOps.swift`'s factories.
179	    private static func op(_ o: [String: Any]) throws -> ReelOp {
180	        func ticks(_ key: String) -> Ticks { (o[key] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value ?? 0 }
181	        switch o["op"] as? String {
182	        case "add_track":
183	            return .addTrack(
184	                index: (o["index"] as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0, name: o["name"] as? String)
185	        case "add_graphic_clip":
186	            return .addGraphicClipRaw(
187	                track: (o["track"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0, at: ticks("at"),
188	                duration: ticks("duration"), name: (o["name"] as? String) ?? "",
189	                props: o["props"], schema: o["schema"])
190	        default:
191	            throw AutoZoom.Refusal(message: "The overlays' plan named an op it does not make.")
192	        }
193	    }
194	}

479	/// D_min(n) = 10n + 25 frames (CU-80): `keyboard-keys.js` presses its last
480	/// keycap at frame `pressAt + 5(n − 1)` = 10n + 9 (`pressAt` = 5n + 14) and
481	/// exits over the clip's last 15 frames, so the last press needs 16 frames
482	/// before the end.
483	pub(crate) fn min_frames(keycaps: usize) -> i64 {
484	    10 * keycaps as i64 + 25
485	}
486	
487	/// A chord's keycap count: its non-empty trimmed `+` tokens, the template's
488	/// own split.
489	fn keycaps(keys: &str) -> usize {
490	    keys.split('+').filter(|t| !t.trim().is_empty()).count()
491	}
492	
493	/// One press in container frames.
494	struct Press {
495	    frame: i64,
496	    keys: String,
497	}
498	
499	/// One overlay in container frames, `[start, end)`.
500	struct Overlay {
501	    start: i64,
502	    end: i64,
503	    keys: String,
504	    n: usize,
505	    count: u32,
506	}
507	
508	/// The overlays CU-80 makes of `presses` (in time order): the overlays,
509	/// the presses dropped and the presses merged.
510	fn lay_out(presses: &[Press], duration: i64, most_late: i64) -> (Vec<Overlay>, u32, u32) {
511	    let (mut out, mut dropped, mut merged): (Vec<Overlay>, u32, u32) = (Vec::new(), 0, 0);
512	    for p in presses {
513	        let n = keycaps(&p.keys);
514	        let length = duration.max(min_frames(n));
515	        let mut start = p.frame;
516	        if let Some(cur) = out.last_mut() {
517	            if p.frame < cur.end {
518	                if p.keys == cur.keys {
519	                    cur.end = cur.end.max(p.frame + duration);
520	                    cur.count += 1;
521	                    merged += 1;
522	                    continue;
523	                }
524	                start = p.frame.max(cur.start + min_frames(cur.n));
525	                if start - p.frame > most_late {
526	                    dropped += 1;
527	                    continue;
528	                }
529	                cur.end = start;
530	            }
531	        }
532	        out.push(Overlay {
533	            start,
534	            end: start + length,
535	            keys: p.keys.clone(),
536	            n,
537	            count: 1,
538	        });
539	    }
540	    (out, dropped, merged)
541	}

543	/// Checks every clip in CU-84's order.
544	fn check(project: &Project, clips: &[u32]) -> Result<(), String> {
545	    for (i, &id) in clips.iter().enumerate() {
546	        if clips[..i].contains(&id) {
547	            return Err(format!("clip {id} is named twice"));
548	        }
549	        let clip = project.require_clip(id)?;
550	        let Source::Media {
551	            media, reversed, ..
552	        } = &clip.source
553	        else {
554	            return Err(format!("clip {id} is not a media clip"));
555	        };
556	        if project
557	            .media(*media)
558	            .and_then(|m| m.cursor.as_ref())
559	            .is_none()
560	        {
561	            return Err(format!("clip {id}'s media {media} has no cursor file"));
562	        }
563	        if *reversed {
564	            return Err(format!(
565	                "clip {id} plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play \
566	                 forward"
567	            ));
568	        }
569	    }
570	    Ok(())
571	}

573	/// The track CU-83 picks for the span `[from, to)`: the id and whether it
574	/// is new.
575	fn track_for(project: &Project, clips: &[u32], span: (Ticks, Ticks)) -> (u32, bool) {
576	    let index_of = |track: u32| project.tracks.iter().position(|t| t.id == track);
577	    let front_of_clips = clips
578	        .iter()
579	        .filter_map(|&id| project.clip(id))
580	        .filter_map(|c| index_of(c.track))
581	        .max()
582	        .unwrap_or(0);
583	    let found = project
584	        .tracks
585	        .iter()
586	        .enumerate()
587	        .rev()
588	        .find(|(_, t)| t.name == TRACK_NAME);
589	    if let Some((index, track)) = found {
590	        let free = !project.clips.iter().any(|c| {
591	            c.track == track.id && c.start < span.1 && span.0 < c.start.saturating_add(c.duration)
592	        });
593	        if index > front_of_clips && !track.locked && !track.hidden && track.matte.is_none() && free
594	        {
595	            return (track.id, false);
596	        }
597	    }
598	    (project.next_id, true)
599	}

601	/// Answers `plan_overlays` (CU-80…CU-84) against `tracks`, one per clip.
602	pub(crate) fn plan_overlays(
603	    tracks: &[&CursorTrack],
604	    project: &Project,
605	    args: PlanOverlaysArgs,
606	) -> Result<Value, String> {
607	    let (lo, hi) = DURATION_RANGE;
608	    if !(args.duration.is_finite() && (lo..=hi).contains(&args.duration)) {
609	        return Err(format!(
610	            "duration is {} s; it runs {lo}–{hi}",
611	            args.duration
612	        ));
613	    }
614	    if let (Some(from), Some(to)) = (args.from, args.to) {
615	        if to <= from {
616	            return Err(format!("to ({to}) must be after from ({from})"));
617	        }
618	    }
619	    if args.clips.is_empty() {
620	        return Err("plan_overlays needs at least one clip".into());
621	    }
622	    if tracks.len() != args.clips.len() {
623	        return Err(format!(
624	            "plan_overlays reads one cursor track per clip; {} clips and {} tracks were given",
625	            args.clips.len(),
626	            tracks.len()
627	        ));
628	    }
629	    check(project, &args.clips)?;
630	    let fps = project.canvas.fps;
631	    let frame = project.frame();
632	    let index = |t: Ticks| time::frame_index(t, fps).unwrap_or(t / frame);
633	    let tick = |i: i64| time::tick_at_frame(i, fps).unwrap_or(i * frame);
634	    let window = (
635	        args.from.unwrap_or(Ticks::MIN),
636	        args.to.unwrap_or(Ticks::MAX),
637	    );
638	    let mut presses: Vec<Press> = Vec::new();
639	    for (i, &id) in args.clips.iter().enumerate() {
640	        let clip = project.require_clip(id)?;
641	        let Some((_, source_in)) = media_in(clip) else {
642	            continue;
643	        };
644	        let length = project.content_length_in_source(clip);
645	        let k = &tracks[i].file().keys.shortcut;
646	        for j in 0..k.t.len() {
647	            let s = us_to_ticks(k.t[j]);
648	            if s < source_in || s >= source_in.saturating_add(length) {
649	                continue;
650	            }
