704	//! Bursts of input in a cursor file (spec §11 CU-25, CU-70): the typing
705	//! stretches an `events` request answers and Auto Zoom anchors on, and the
706	//! scroll bursts that end an Auto Zoom visit, by CU7's figures. CU9b reads
707	//! the same stretches. Both are one run finder with their own figures.
708	
709	/// Marks closer than this belong to one stretch (strictly under 1.0 s).
710	pub const TYPING_GAP_US: i64 = 1_000_000;
711	/// The fewest marks a stretch holds.
712	pub const TYPING_MIN_MARKS: usize = 3;
713	/// Wheel events closer than this belong to one burst (strictly under 1.0 s).
714	pub const SCROLL_GAP_US: i64 = 1_000_000;
715	/// The fewest wheel events a burst holds.
716	pub const SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS: usize = 3;
717	
718	/// Each run of `t` (µs, in order) whose neighbours are less than `gap`
719	/// apart and which holds at least `min` entries, as (first, last, count).
720	fn runs(t: &[i64], gap: i64, min: usize) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
721	    let mut out = Vec::new();
722	    let mut start = 0;
723	    for i in 1..=t.len() {
724	        if i == t.len() || t[i] - t[i - 1] >= gap {
725	            if i - start >= min {
726	                out.push((t[start], t[i - 1], i - start));
727	            }
728	            start = i;
729	        }
730	    }
731	    out
732	}
733	
734	/// The typing stretches of `t` (the `typed` marks' µs, in order): each run
735	/// of marks less than `TYPING_GAP_US` apart holding at least
736	/// `TYPING_MIN_MARKS`, as (first mark, last mark, marks).
737	pub(crate) fn typing_stretches(t: &[i64]) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
738	    runs(t, TYPING_GAP_US, TYPING_MIN_MARKS)
739	}
740	
741	/// The scroll bursts of `t` (the `scrolls`' µs, in order): each run of
742	/// wheel events less than `SCROLL_GAP_US` apart holding at least
743	/// `SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS`, as (first, last, events).
744	pub(crate) fn scroll_bursts(t: &[i64]) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
745	    runs(t, SCROLL_GAP_US, SCROLL_MIN_EVENTS)
746	}
747	//! Auto Zoom's visits (spec §11 CU-70): anchors in container time become
748	//! visits, and visits become planned zoom-ins, pans, follow pans and zoom
749	//! backs, still in container time and not yet on any clip. Pure: no
750	//! `Project`, no cursor file — `cursor_zoom.rs` maps the file into
751	//! [`Anchor`]s, scroll-burst starts, barriers and a cursor sampler, and
752	//! moves what comes back onto clips (CU-74).
753	//!
754	//! Positions are in P: source pixels from the centre of the UNCROPPED
755	//! picture, y down. A region is centred on its aim and clamped inside the
756	//! cropped rect ([`Frame`]); `cursor_zoom.rs` turns P into Q per clip.
757	//!
758	//! **Barriers** are cuts a hold may not cross (a cut into a clip that was
759	//! not given, or into one whose kept action meets the hold) and the run's
760	//! end. No visit spans one; a visit whose zoom back would end past one is
761	//! closed with a zoom back ending at it, counted when the barrier is a cut.
762	
763	use crate::time::{Ticks, TIMESCALE};
764	
765	/// A zoom back's length: 0.8 s.
766	pub(crate) const BACK: Ticks = TIMESCALE * 8 / 10;
767	/// A follow pan's length: 0.5 s.
768	const FOLLOW_PAN: Ticks = TIMESCALE / 2;
769	/// How long the cursor stays outside the inner 70 % before a follow pan.
770	const FOLLOW_OUTSIDE: Ticks = TIMESCALE * 3 / 10;
771	/// At most one follow pan a second, start to start.
772	const FOLLOW_EVERY: Ticks = TIMESCALE;
773	/// The follow sampler's step: 10 Hz.
774	const SAMPLE: Ticks = TIMESCALE / 10;
775	/// A zoom back ending under this before the next zoom-in starts merges.
776	const MERGE_GAP: Ticks = TIMESCALE;
777	/// Half the inner part an anchor must leave to pan: 60 %.
778	const ANCHOR_HALF: f64 = 0.3;
779	/// Half the inner part the followed cursor must leave: 70 %.
780	const FOLLOW_HALF: f64 = 0.35;
781	
782	/// One anchor: a down click, or a typing stretch aimed per CU-72.
783	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
784	pub(crate) struct Anchor {
785	    /// Container time of the click, or of the stretch's first mark.
786	    pub t: Ticks,
787	    /// Container time the activity runs to (`t` for a click).
788	    pub end: Ticks,
789	    /// Where it aims, in P.
790	    pub p: (f64, f64),
791	}
792	
793	/// The region's size and the cropped rect it is clamped inside, in P.
794	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
795	pub(crate) struct Frame {
796	    pub size: (f64, f64),
797	    pub min: (f64, f64),
798	    pub max: (f64, f64),
799	}
800	
801	impl Frame {
802	    /// The region centre for an aim: clamped so the region stays inside
803	    /// the cropped rect, centred on an axis it exceeds.
804	    pub(crate) fn clamp(&self, p: (f64, f64)) -> (f64, f64) {
805	        let axis = |v: f64, size: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64| {
806	            if size >= hi - lo {
807	                (lo + hi) / 2.0
808	            } else {
809	                v.clamp(lo + size / 2.0, hi - size / 2.0)
810	            }
811	        };
812	        (
813	            axis(p.0, self.size.0, self.min.0, self.max.0),
814	            axis(p.1, self.size.1, self.min.1, self.max.1),
815	        )
816	    }
817	
818	    fn outside(&self, centre: (f64, f64), p: (f64, f64), half: f64) -> bool {
819	        (p.0 - centre.0).abs() > half * self.size.0 || (p.1 - centre.1).abs() > half * self.size.1
820	    }
821	}
822	
823	/// The figures a plan is made with.
824	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
825	pub(crate) struct Timing {
826	    pub lead: Ticks,
827	    pub stay: Ticks,
828	    pub follow: bool,
829	    /// One frame of the grid: a pan shorter than this is not planned.
830	    pub frame: Ticks,
831	}
832	
833	/// What a planned action does.
834	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
835	pub(crate) enum Kind {
836	    In,
837	    Pan,
838	    Follow,
839	    Back,
840	}
841	
842	impl Kind {
843	    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
844	        match self {
845	            Kind::In => "in",
846	            Kind::Pan => "pan",
847	            Kind::Follow => "follow",
848	            Kind::Back => "back",
849	        }
850	    }
851	}
852	
853	/// One planned action in container time; `aim` is the region's centre in
854	/// P, `None` for a zoom back.
855	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
856	pub(crate) struct Planned {
857	    pub from: Ticks,
858	    pub to: Ticks,
859	    pub kind: Kind,
860	    pub aim: Option<(f64, f64)>,
861	}
862	
863	/// A time no hold crosses; `counted` for a cut, not for the run's end.
864	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
865	pub(crate) struct Barrier {
866	    pub at: Ticks,
867	    pub counted: bool,
868	}
869	
870	/// The plan of one run.
871	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
872	pub(crate) struct Plan {
873	    pub actions: Vec<Planned>,
874	    pub visits: usize,
875	    pub closed: usize,
876	    /// Each hold's span, its zoom-in's start to its zoom back's end.
877	    pub holds: Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)>,
878	}
879	
880	struct Visit {
881	    anchors: Vec<Anchor>,
882	    last: Ticks,
883	    back: Ticks,
884	}
885	
886	/// Anchors (any order), scroll-burst starts, barriers, the figures and the
887	/// frame, and the cursor in P at a container time → the run's plan.
888	pub(crate) fn plan(
889	    mut anchors: Vec<Anchor>,
890	    bursts: &[Ticks],
891	    barriers: &[Barrier],
892	    timing: Timing,
893	    frame: Frame,
894	    cursor: &dyn Fn(Ticks) -> Option<(f64, f64)>,
895	) -> Plan {
896	    anchors.sort_by_key(|a| a.t);
897	    let barrier_in = |lo: Ticks, hi: Ticks| barriers.iter().any(|b| lo < b.at && b.at <= hi);
898	    let mut visits: Vec<Visit> = Vec::new();
899	    for a in anchors {
900	        let joins = visits.last().is_some_and(|v| {
901	            let prev = v.anchors.last().map_or(a.t, |p| p.t);
902	            a.t <= v.last + timing.stay
903	                && !bursts.iter().any(|&b| v.last < b && b < a.t)
904	                && !barrier_in(prev, a.t)
905	        });
906	        match visits.last_mut() {
907	            Some(v) if joins => {
908	                v.last = v.last.max(a.end);
909	                v.anchors.push(a);
910	            }
911	            _ => visits.push(Visit {
912	                anchors: vec![a],
913	                last: a.end,
914	                back: 0,
915	            }),
916	        }
917	    }
918	    let mut out = Plan {
919	        visits: visits.len(),
920	        ..Plan::default()
921	    };
922	    // Each visit's zoom back: Stay after its last activity, or the first
923	    // scroll burst after its last anchor, closed at the next barrier.
924	    let mut closed_by = vec![false; visits.len()];
925	    for (i, v) in visits.iter_mut().enumerate() {
926	        let last_anchor = v.anchors.last().map_or(0, |a| a.t);
927	        let mut back = v.last + timing.stay;
928	        if let Some(&b) = bursts.iter().find(|&&b| b > last_anchor) {
929	            back = back.min(b);
930	        }
931	        if let Some(bar) = barriers.iter().find(|b| b.at > last_anchor) {
932	            if back + BACK > bar.at {
933	                back = bar.at - BACK;
934	                closed_by[i] = true;
935	                if bar.counted {
936	                    out.closed += 1;
937	                }
938	            }
939	        }
940	        v.back = back;
941	    }
942	    // Chains: a visit whose zoom back would end under MERGE_GAP before the
943	    // next one's zoom-in starts runs on into it with one pan.
944	    let mut chains: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();
945	    for i in 0..visits.len() {
946	        let merge = i > 0 && !closed_by[i - 1] && {
947	            let (v, w) = (&visits[i - 1], &visits[i]);
948	            let next = w.anchors[0].t;
949	            let prev = v.anchors.last().map_or(next, |a| a.t);
950	            next - timing.lead - (v.back + BACK) < MERGE_GAP && !barrier_in(prev, next)
951	        };
952	        match chains.last_mut() {
953	            Some(chain) if merge => chain.push(i),
954	            _ => chains.push(vec![i]),
955	        }
956	    }
957	    for chain in chains {
958	        plan_chain(&chain, &visits, timing, frame, cursor, &mut out);
959	    }
960	    out
961	}
962	
963	/// One hold: a zoom-in, the anchors' pans (a merged visit's first anchor
964	/// always pans), follow pans, a zoom back.
965	fn plan_chain(
966	    chain: &[usize],
967	    visits: &[Visit],
968	    timing: Timing,
969	    frame: Frame,
970	    cursor: &dyn Fn(Ticks) -> Option<(f64, f64)>,
971	    out: &mut Plan,
972	) {
973	    let mut anchors: Vec<(Anchor, bool)> = Vec::new();
974	    for (k, &i) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
975	        for (j, a) in visits[i].anchors.iter().enumerate() {
976	            anchors.push((*a, k > 0 && j == 0));
977	        }
978	    }
979	    let back = visits[chain[chain.len() - 1]].back;
980	    let first = anchors[0].0;
981	    let mut region = frame.clamp(first.p);
982	    let hold_start = first.t - timing.lead;
983	    out.actions.push(Planned {
984	        from: hold_start,
985	        to: first.t,
986	        kind: Kind::In,
987	        aim: Some(region),
988	    });
989	    let mut busy = first.t;
990	    let mut next = 1;
991	    let mut t = first.t;
992	    let mut outside_since: Option<Ticks> = None;
993	    let mut last_follow: Option<Ticks> = None;
994	    loop {
995	        while next < anchors.len() && anchors[next].0.t - timing.lead <= t {
996	            let (a, forced) = anchors[next];
997	            if forced || frame.outside(region, a.p, ANCHOR_HALF) {
998	                let start = (a.t - timing.lead).max(busy);
999	                if a.t - start >= timing.frame {
1000	                    region = frame.clamp(a.p);
1001	                    out.actions.push(Planned {
1002	                        from: start,
1003	                        to: a.t,
1004	                        kind: Kind::Pan,
1005	                        aim: Some(region),
1006	                    });
1007	                    busy = a.t;
1008	                }
1009	            }
1010	            outside_since = None;
1011	            next += 1;
1012	        }
1013	        if t >= back {
1014	            break;
1015	        }
1016	        let watched = timing.follow && t >= busy;
1017	        match watched.then(|| cursor(t)).flatten() {
1018	            Some(p) if frame.outside(region, p, FOLLOW_HALF) => {
1019	                let since = *outside_since.get_or_insert(t);
1020	                let end = t + FOLLOW_PAN;
1021	                let free = !anchors[next..]
1022	                    .iter()
1023	                    .any(|(a, _)| a.t - timing.lead < end && t < a.t);
1024	                if t - since >= FOLLOW_OUTSIDE
1025	                    && last_follow.is_none_or(|l| t - l >= FOLLOW_EVERY)
1026	                    && end <= back
1027	                    && free
1028	                {
1029	                    region = frame.clamp(p);
1030	                    out.actions.push(Planned {
1031	                        from: t,
1032	                        to: end,
1033	                        kind: Kind::Follow,
1034	                        aim: Some(region),
1035	                    });
1036	                    busy = end;
1037	                    last_follow = Some(t);
1038	                    outside_since = None;
1039	                }
1040	            }
1041	            _ => outside_since = None,
1042	        }
1043	        t += SAMPLE;
1044	    }
1045	    let from = back.max(busy);
1046	    let to = back + BACK;
1047	    if to - from >= timing.frame {
1048	        out.actions.push(Planned {
1049	            from,
1050	            to,
1051	            kind: Kind::Back,
1052	            aim: None,
1053	        });
1054	    }
1055	    out.holds.push((hold_start, to));
1056	}

content.content:
### Enhancing the microphone

With **Enhance the microphone when it lands** ticked, the recording lands exactly as it would otherwise, and then Frame Job runs [Enhance Voice](audio.md#enhance-voice) on the microphone's clips: each stretch's microphone file, or a voice-over's files. It never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio. Enhance Voice needs the microphone's sound analysed first (its loudness and its speech), which takes a few seconds after the files land; it then runs under the **Measuring Sound** sheet, at Normalize's target loudness, and its settings appear in the clip's Sound tab.

It's its own undo step, **Enhance Voice**, after the landing's. Edit ▸ Undo first reads **Undo Enhance Voice**, which takes the processing off and keeps the recording; in an open project the next undo is **Undo Add Recording**. In a new project the next is the landing's own step (**Add Microphone**, **Add Camera and Microphone** or **Add Recording Segments**), or nothing when the recording is a single file, which is the project itself.

It waits while you drag in the project, while a sheet is up on its window, or while you're inside another nest than the one the recording landed in. Pressing **Cancel** on the Measuring Sound sheet leaves the clips as they landed. When there's nothing to enhance (a silent microphone, for example), or the sound wasn't analysed within 5 minutes, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector, and you can select the clip and choose **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** yourself.

### When it lands

The three boxes under **When it lands:** polish a screen recording once it's in the project. The recording lands exactly as it would otherwise, any [Enhance the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone) runs first, and then, in this order, each ticked box runs its command on the recording's screen clips (the clips of each stretch's movie that has a cursor file):

1. **Zoom in on clicks** runs **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** with the values the Auto Zoom sheet last used, Zoom on typing on when the recording has typing.
2. **Show shortcuts** runs **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** (bottom, dark).
3. **Speed up typing** runs **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** with the values its sheet last used, once the microphone's speech has been detected, so typing you talk over keeps its pace.

Zooms are planned on the clips before the speed-up splits them, and the speed-up leaves each overlay at its pace. No sheet comes up. Each is its own undo step, **Auto Zoom**, **Add Shortcut Overlays** and **Speed Up Typing**, after the landing's (and after **Enhance Voice**), so Edit ▸ Undo takes them off one at a time, last first, and keeps the recording.

Like Enhance, each waits while you drag in the project, while a sheet is up on its window, or while you're inside another nest than the one the recording landed in. When a command is refused, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector and the next one still runs; that includes a speed-up that would leave a clip silent above ×12, which this never applies without asking (choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** yourself to be asked). When the project stays busy, or the speech isn't detected, for 5 minutes, that is said there too and the rest don't run; select the clips and choose the command yourself. A recording with no cursor file, and a command with nothing to do (no click, no shortcut, no typing stretch long enough), change nothing and say nothing.

Show shortcuts and Speed up typing need **Record shortcuts**: without it the cursor file holds no shortcut and no typing.

### When the panel comes back

A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Press ⌥⌘N to open it again. The panel returns on its own, with a note, only when it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to say, for example:

- the recording was stopped from macOS's indicator, or the display slept or went away, or the camera stopped on its own
- the project you chose had closed, so it opened as a new project
- a stretch's movie couldn't be read (for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume) and was left out. Its microphone file still lands on the Microphone track where the picture would have been, and the next picture starts after that gap. The note names the left-out file and the files it kept. Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
- the files didn't finish writing within 10 s of Stop. The note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the movie and microphone files kept on disk.
- the microphone stopped or failed (the picture still landed)

input.content:
---
title: "Auto Zoom"
description: "Zoom a screen recording in where things happen, planned from its cursor file, with every zoom left as an ordinary action you can change."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Auto Zoom moves a screen recording in where things happen. It reads the recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), arrives at each click as it happens, stays while you keep working there, and zooms back out once you stop.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
  where="Zoom in on clicks, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
  tools="auto_zoom"
  needs="A recording with a cursor file. Nothing else: it plans from that file on your Mac, with no picture analysis and no key."
/>

## Zoom a recording

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips of a screen recording. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** is available when every selected clip is a movie with a cursor file, and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" and **Zoom** is dimmed until they're read and there's a plan.

3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls). The line under them [says what you'd get](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).

4. Choose **Zoom**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The whole plan is one undo step, **Auto Zoom**.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Zoom:** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× | 1.25 to 4× |
| **Arrive:** | How long the zoom takes, in seconds. It starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click. | 0.6 s | 0.2 to 2 s |
| **Stay:** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it starts back out. | 2.5 s | 0.5 to 10 s |
| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | On | |
| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing as well as clicks. | On when the recording holds typing | |
| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. | Off | |
| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur. | On | |

The number fields take up to two decimal places, and each value is held to its range.

### Follow the cursor while zoomed

When the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the zoomed view for 0.3 s, the view makes a half-second pan to it. It makes at most one of these pans a second, and none that would run into the zoom back out or a pan to a coming click.

### Zoom on typing

A stretch of typing is at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. The zoom arrives at the first key and aims at the last click before the stretch, because the typing marks say when you typed, not where. With no click before it, the zoom aims at where the pointer was.

**Zoom on typing** is greyed out when the recording holds no such stretch. A recording only holds typing if it was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, which needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission.

### Replace existing zooms

Off, your own zooms stay, and a planned zoom that would meet one is [left out](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions). On, the selected clips' zooms go first. A zoom here is any action that changes only a clip's scale and position, so it takes hand-made zooms from [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) as well as Auto Zoom's own. A speed change, a fade or any other action stays.

### Motion blur

The zoomed clips get a 180° shutter in the same undo step, so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. Only clips that actually get a zoom are touched. A clip that already has a [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) keeps its own, and unticking the box doesn't take one away.

## What the sheet tells you

The line under the controls updates when you tick a box or leave a number field.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "5 zooms in 2 visits." | What **Zoom** would make. Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out counts as one zoom, so a click with nothing after it is two. |
| "1 dropped where an action is already set." | Follows the line above: that many planned zooms [met an action](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions) already on the clip and were left out. |
| "0 zooms in 0 visits." | Nothing in the clips' played part calls for a zoom. **Zoom** closes the sheet and changes nothing, unless **Replace existing zooms** is on, when it still removes the clips' zooms. |
| "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas…" | See [A clip placed smaller than the canvas](#a-clip-placed-smaller-than-the-canvas). |
| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Auto Zoom plans only clips that play forward." | Auto Zoom won't plan a reversed clip. |
| "Clip 12 has no picture." | The selection includes a clip with sound only. Select the picture. |
| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |

With any of the last five, **Zoom** stays dimmed.

### A clip placed smaller than the canvas

Auto Zoom won't plan a clip that sits smaller than the canvas, such as a screen beside a camera or a picture in picture, because a zoom would fill the canvas. The sheet says "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto Zoom inside the nest."

Do what it says: [nest the clip](/editing/nests/), open the nest and run Auto Zoom there. The zooms then fill the nest, and the nest keeps its place on the canvas.

## How a visit is planned

Auto Zoom groups the recording's activity into visits, and each visit becomes a run of moves.

- **A visit starts** at a click with any button, or at a stretch of typing when **Zoom on typing** is on.
- **The zoom in** ends on that first click or key, and starts **Arrive:** seconds before it.
- **A later click** within **Stay:** of the last activity joins the visit. If it falls outside the middle 60 % of the view, the view pans to it, arriving on the click.
- **The zoom back out** starts **Stay:** seconds after the last click or the last key of a typing stretch, and takes 0.8 s.
- **Scrolling ends a visit.** Three or more wheel events under a second apart count as scrolling, and the zoom back out starts where they start. A click after that begins a new visit.
- **Visits close together run on.** When one visit would finish zooming out less than a second before the next starts zooming in, the view pans across instead.

The view keeps the canvas's shape and never shows past the edge of the picture, or of a crop on the clip. Near a corner it stops at the corner, so the click sits off centre.

Only what plays counts. A click in a part you've trimmed away is ignored, and everything is placed through the clip's speed and any speed ramp.

## The zooms are ordinary actions

Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out is a normal [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/), the same kind [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) makes. Each is snapped to the frame grid and eases in and out. You can [move, resize or remove](/motion/change-an-action/) any of them, or [change what it animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

Actions on a clip can't overlap, so a planned zoom that would meet one already there is left out and counted in the sheet. This goes piece by piece, so a visit can lose its zoom in and keep its zoom back out. Check those visits by eye.

To try different settings after you've applied a plan, undo it, or run Auto Zoom again with **Replace existing zooms** on. Run again without it and the new plan meets the old one, and most of it is dropped.

## Across a split

The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording: clips side by side on one track, from the same file, each carrying on where the last stopped.

- Every zoom back out returns to the first half's placement.
- No zoom crosses a cut. One that would is moved to one side of it.
- A zoom held across a cut carries into the next half, which starts already zoomed. Frame Job does this by setting that half's own scale and position.
- If that half wasn't selected, or has an action of its own during the zoom, the zoom goes back out at the cut instead.

With **Replace existing zooms** on, a later half left zoomed by an earlier run goes back to the first half's placement, unless an action you've kept moves it.

## What Auto Zoom remembers

Frame Job remembers **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** from one use to the next. A value is kept only if you changed it and then chose **Zoom**. **Cancel** keeps nothing.

**Zoom on typing** is never remembered. It's ticked whenever the recording holds typing.

## Zoom when a recording lands

**Zoom in on clicks**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), runs Auto Zoom by itself on a finished screen recording, with the values the sheet last used and no sheet. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## Good to know

- A click right at the start of a clip has no room before it. The zoom in starts on the clip's first frame and takes its full **Arrive:** time, so it finishes just after the click.
- **Zoom:** multiplies the size the clip is placed at, so a clip already scaled up goes further in than the number suggests.
- If a selected clip isn't a movie with a cursor file, the menu item is dimmed.

## With an agent

`auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments. An agent can also limit the plan to a stretch of the timeline, and set a motion blur other than 50 %. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

title: "Auto Zoom"
description: "Zoom a screen recording in where things happen, planned from its cursor file, with every zoom left as an ordinary action you can change."

  menu="Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
  where="Zoom in on clicks, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"

1. Select one or more clips of a screen recording. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** is available when every selected clip is a movie with a cursor file, and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" and **Zoom** is dimmed until they're read and there's a plan.

3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls). The line under them [says what you'd get](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).

4. Choose **Zoom**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The whole plan is one undo step, **Auto Zoom**.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Zoom:** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× | 1.25 to 4× |
| **Arrive:** | How long the zoom takes, in seconds. It starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click. | 0.6 s | 0.2 to 2 s |
| **Stay:** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it starts back out. | 2.5 s | 0.5 to 10 s |
| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | On | |
| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing as well as clicks. | On when the recording holds typing | |
| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. | Off | |
| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur. | On | |

The number fields take up to two decimal places, and each value is held to its range.

### Follow the cursor while zoomed

When the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the zoomed view for 0.3 s, the view makes a half-second pan to it. It makes at most one of these pans a second, and none that would run into the zoom back out or a pan to a coming click.

### Zoom on typing

A stretch of typing is at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. The zoom arrives at the first key and aims at the last click before the stretch, because the typing marks say when you typed, not where. With no click before it, the zoom aims at where the pointer was.

**Zoom on typing** is greyed out when the recording holds no such stretch. A recording only holds typing if it was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, which needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission.

### Replace existing zooms

Off, your own zooms stay, and a planned zoom that would meet one is [left out](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions). On, the selected clips' zooms go first. A zoom here is any action that changes only a clip's scale and position, so it takes hand-made zooms from [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) as well as Auto Zoom's own. A speed change, a fade or any other action stays.

### Motion blur

The zoomed clips get a 180° shutter in the same undo step, so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. Only clips that actually get a zoom are touched. A clip that already has a [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) keeps its own, and unticking the box doesn't take one away.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |

| "0 zooms in 0 visits." | Nothing in the clips' played part calls for a zoom. **Zoom** closes the sheet and changes nothing, unless **Replace existing zooms** is on, when it still removes the clips' zooms. |
| "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas…" | See [A clip placed smaller than the canvas](#a-clip-placed-smaller-than-the-canvas). |
| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Auto Zoom plans only clips that play forward." | Auto Zoom won't plan a reversed clip. |
| "Clip 12 has no picture." | The selection includes a clip with sound only. Select the picture. |
| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |

With **Replace existing zooms** on, a later half left zoomed by an earlier run goes back to the first half's placement, unless an action you've kept moves it.

---
title: "Shortcut overlays"
description: "Show each keyboard shortcut you pressed while recording as animated keycaps on screen, at the moment you pressed it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Shortcut overlays show a viewer what you pressed. Each keyboard shortcut in a screen recording appears as keycaps on screen at the moment you pressed it, so nobody has to guess how you did that.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
  where="Show shortcuts, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
  tools="add_shortcut_overlays"
  needs="A recording made with Record shortcuts on, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission. No key: it runs on your Mac."
/>

## Add the overlays

<Steps>

1. Make the recording with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Only shortcuts are recorded, never what you typed.

2. Select one or more clips of the recording. The menu item is available when every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**.

</Steps>

There's no sheet. Frame Job reads the cursor files, with the item dimmed while it does, and places one **Keyboard keys** graphic clip per shortcut on a [Shortcuts track](#the-shortcuts-track). Each sits at the bottom of the picture in the dark theme and shows for 1.5 s.

The whole change is one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. If some shortcuts couldn't be shown, or nothing could be added, a [sheet says so](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).

## What an overlay shows

The keycaps pop in one after another, each is pressed in turn, and the group fades out at the end of the clip. ⌘, ⇧, ⌥, ⌃ and the arrow keys are drawn as symbols, a single character as its capital, and a named key such as `return` or `f5` as its word.

## How overlays are timed

**Where it starts.** An overlay starts on the frame where the press plays, following the clip's speed and any speed ramp. Only the part of a clip that plays counts, so a shortcut in a part you've trimmed away gets no overlay.

**How long it lasts.** Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out. That minimum is (10 × keycaps + 25) frames at the project's frame rate:

| Keycaps | Minimum at 30 fps | Minimum at 60 fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 45 frames, 1.5 s | 45 frames, 0.75 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
| 3 | 55 frames, about 1.83 s | 55 frames, about 0.92 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
| 4 | 65 frames, about 2.17 s | 65 frames, about 1.08 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |

**When you repeat a shortcut.** Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends doesn't make a second overlay. The first stays up until 1.5 s after the last press and carries a label under the keycaps: "×2", "×3" and so on.

**When shortcuts come close together.** Overlays never overlap. A different shortcut pressed while one is showing takes over as soon as the first has had its minimum, and the first ends there. If that would show the new shortcut more than half a second late, it's left out, and a sheet says how many were.

## The Shortcuts track

Overlays go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when that track is usable, and otherwise on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. To be usable, the track must:

- be in front of every selected clip's track
- be unlocked and shown
- not be a [matte](/canvas/mattes/)
- have nothing on it from the first overlay's start to the last overlay's end

## Change an overlay

Each overlay is an ordinary graphic clip. Move, trim or delete it on the timeline, and change its keys, label, theme, position or accent colour in its [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). To change them all at once, select them first.

The overlays are drawn by the project's own copy of the bundled [Keyboard keys template](/graphics/templates/). Frame Job writes that copy into the project's graphics the first time something is placed, and reuses it after. If you've [edited that copy](/graphics/edit-a-module/), it leaves your version alone and writes a fresh one beside it for new overlays.

Undo takes the clips away but not the copy, which stays in the project's graphics for next time.

## What the sheet tells you

An informational sheet comes up when something didn't go as asked. Only the "too close" sheet comes with a change to the project.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added." | The part of the recording that plays holds no shortcut. Check that the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** on. |
| "1 shortcut came too close to show." | The overlays were added, without that many. With more it reads "3 shortcuts came too close to show." |
| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play forward." | Frame Job won't place overlays for a reversed clip. |
| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
| "The project changed while the cursor files were read, so no overlay was added. Choose Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays again." | You edited the project, or opened or left a nest, while the files were being read. Nothing was added. |

## Show shortcuts when a recording lands

**Show shortcuts**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), adds the overlays by itself on a finished screen recording, at the bottom in the dark theme. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## Good to know

- Add the overlays before you run [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/). It keeps each overlay on a Shortcuts track at normal speed.
- Running the command again on the same clips doesn't replace the overlays. The Shortcuts track isn't free any more, so you get a second Shortcuts track with the same overlays on it. Undo first if you want to start over.

## With an agent

`add_shortcut_overlays` places the same overlays. An agent can also choose how long each one shows, from 0.5 to 10 s, put them at the centre or top of the picture, use the light theme, and limit them to a stretch of the timeline. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

## Related

- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)

---
title: "Auto Zoom"
description: "Zoom a screen recording in where things happen, planned from its cursor file, with every zoom left as an ordinary action you can change."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Auto Zoom moves a screen recording in where things happen. It reads the recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), arrives at each click as it happens, stays while you keep working there, and zooms back out once you stop.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
  where="Zoom in on clicks, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
  tools="auto_zoom"
  needs="A recording with a cursor file. Nothing else: it plans from that file on your Mac, with no picture analysis and no key."
/>

## Zoom a recording

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips of a screen recording. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** is available when every selected clip is a movie with a cursor file, and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" and **Zoom** is dimmed until they're read and there's a plan.

3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls). The line under them [says what you'd get](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).

4. Choose **Zoom**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The whole plan is one undo step, **Auto Zoom**.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Zoom:** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× | 1.25 to 4× |
| **Arrive:** | How long the zoom takes, in seconds. It starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click. | 0.6 s | 0.2 to 2 s |
| **Stay:** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it starts back out. | 2.5 s | 0.5 to 10 s |
| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | On | |
| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing as well as clicks. | On when the recording holds typing | |
| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. | Off | |
| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur. | On | |

The number fields take up to two decimal places, and each value is held to its range.

### Follow the cursor while zoomed

When the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the zoomed view for 0.3 s, the view makes a half-second pan to it. It makes at most one of these pans a second, and none that would run into the zoom back out or a pan to a coming click.

### Zoom on typing

A stretch of typing is at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. The zoom arrives at the first key and aims at the last click before the stretch, because the typing marks say when you typed, not where. With no click before it, the zoom aims at where the pointer was.

**Zoom on typing** is greyed out when the recording holds no such stretch. A recording only holds typing if it was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, which needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission.

### Replace existing zooms

Off, your own zooms stay, and a planned zoom that would meet one is [left out](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions). On, the selected clips' zooms go first. A zoom here is any action that changes only a clip's scale and position, so it takes hand-made zooms from [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) as well as Auto Zoom's own. A speed change, a fade or any other action stays.

### Motion blur

The zoomed clips get a 180° shutter in the same undo step, so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. Only clips that actually get a zoom are touched. A clip that already has a [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) keeps its own, and unticking the box doesn't take one away.

## What the sheet tells you

The line under the controls updates when you tick a box or leave a number field.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "5 zooms in 2 visits." | What **Zoom** would make. Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out counts as one zoom, so a click with nothing after it is two. |
| "1 dropped where an action is already set." | Follows the line above: that many planned zooms [met an action](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions) already on the clip and were left out. |
| "0 zooms in 0 visits." | Nothing in the clips' played part calls for a zoom. **Zoom** closes the sheet and changes nothing, unless **Replace existing zooms** is on, when it still removes the clips' zooms. |
| "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas…" | See [A clip placed smaller than the canvas](#a-clip-placed-smaller-than-the-canvas). |
| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Auto Zoom plans only clips that play forward." | Auto Zoom won't plan a reversed clip. |
| "Clip 12 has no picture." | The selection includes a clip with sound only. Select the picture. |
| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |

With any of the last five, **Zoom** stays dimmed.

### A clip placed smaller than the canvas

Auto Zoom won't plan a clip that sits smaller than the canvas, such as a screen beside a camera or a picture in picture, because a zoom would fill the canvas. The sheet says "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto Zoom inside the nest."

Do what it says: [nest the clip](/editing/nests/), open the nest and run Auto Zoom there. The zooms then fill the nest, and the nest keeps its place on the canvas.

## How a visit is planned

Auto Zoom groups the recording's activity into visits, and each visit becomes a run of moves.

- **A visit starts** at a click with any button, or at a stretch of typing when **Zoom on typing** is on.
- **The zoom in** ends on that first click or key, and starts **Arrive:** seconds before it.
- **A later click** within **Stay:** of the last activity joins the visit. If it falls outside the middle 60 % of the view, the view pans to it, arriving on the click.
- **The zoom back out** starts **Stay:** seconds after the last click or the last key of a typing stretch, and takes 0.8 s.
- **Scrolling ends a visit.** Three or more wheel events under a second apart count as scrolling, and the zoom back out starts where they start. A click after that begins a new visit.
- **Visits close together run on.** When one visit would finish zooming out less than a second before the next starts zooming in, the view pans across instead.

The view keeps the canvas's shape and never shows past the edge of the picture, or of a crop on the clip. Near a corner it stops at the corner, so the click sits off centre.

Only what plays counts. A click in a part you've trimmed away is ignored, and everything is placed through the clip's speed and any speed ramp.

## The zooms are ordinary actions

Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out is a normal [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/), the same kind [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) makes. Each is snapped to the frame grid and eases in and out. You can [move, resize or remove](/motion/change-an-action/) any of them, or [change what it animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).

Actions on a clip can't overlap, so a planned zoom that would meet one already there is left out and counted in the sheet. This goes piece by piece, so a visit can lose its zoom in and keep its zoom back out. Check those visits by eye.

To try different settings after you've applied a plan, undo it, or run Auto Zoom again with **Replace existing zooms** on. Run again without it and the new plan meets the old one, and most of it is dropped.

## Across a split

The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording: clips side by side on one track, from the same file, each carrying on where the last stopped.

- Every zoom back out returns to the first half's placement.
- No zoom crosses a cut. One that would is moved to one side of it.
- A zoom held across a cut carries into the next half, which starts already zoomed. Frame Job does this by setting that half's own scale and position.
- If that half wasn't selected, or has an action of its own during the zoom, the zoom goes back out at the cut instead.

With **Replace existing zooms** on, a later half left zoomed by an earlier run goes back to the first half's placement, unless an action you've kept moves it.

## What Auto Zoom remembers

Frame Job remembers **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** from one use to the next. A value is kept only if you changed it and then chose **Zoom**. **Cancel** keeps nothing.

**Zoom on typing** is never remembered. It's ticked whenever the recording holds typing.

## Zoom when a recording lands

**Zoom in on clicks**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), runs Auto Zoom by itself on a finished screen recording, with the values the sheet last used and no sheet. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## Good to know

- A click right at the start of a clip has no room before it. The zoom in starts on the clip's first frame and takes its full **Arrive:** time, so it finishes just after the click.
- **Zoom:** multiplies the size the clip is placed at, so a clip already scaled up goes further in than the number suggests.
- If a selected clip isn't a movie with a cursor file, the menu item is dimmed.

## With an agent

`auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments. An agent can also limit the plan to a stretch of the timeline, and set a motion blur other than 50 %. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

## Related

- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/)
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)
- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)

---
title: "Shortcut overlays"
description: "Show each keyboard shortcut you pressed while recording as animated keycaps on screen, at the moment you pressed it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Shortcut overlays show a viewer what you pressed. Each keyboard shortcut in a screen recording appears as keycaps on screen at the moment you pressed it, so nobody has to guess how you did that.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
  where="Show shortcuts, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
  tools="add_shortcut_overlays"
  needs="A recording made with Record shortcuts on, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission. No key: it runs on your Mac."
/>

## Add the overlays

<Steps>

1. Make the recording with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Only shortcuts are recorded, never what you typed.

2. Select one or more clips of the recording. The menu item is available when every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**.

</Steps>

There's no sheet. Frame Job reads the cursor files, with the item dimmed while it does, and places one **Keyboard keys** graphic clip per shortcut on a [Shortcuts track](#the-shortcuts-track). Each sits at the bottom of the picture in the dark theme and shows for 1.5 s.

The whole change is one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. If some shortcuts couldn't be shown, or nothing could be added, a [sheet says so](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).

## What an overlay shows

The keycaps pop in one after another, each is pressed in turn, and the group fades out at the end of the clip. ⌘, ⇧, ⌥, ⌃ and the arrow keys are drawn as symbols, a single character as its capital, and a named key such as `return` or `f5` as its word.

## How overlays are timed

**Where it starts.** An overlay starts on the frame where the press plays, following the clip's speed and any speed ramp. Only the part of a clip that plays counts, so a shortcut in a part you've trimmed away gets no overlay.

**How long it lasts.** Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out. That minimum is (10 × keycaps + 25) frames at the project's frame rate:

| Keycaps | Minimum at 30 fps | Minimum at 60 fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 45 frames, 1.5 s | 45 frames, 0.75 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
| 3 | 55 frames, about 1.83 s | 55 frames, about 0.92 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
| 4 | 65 frames, about 2.17 s | 65 frames, about 1.08 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |

**When you repeat a shortcut.** Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends doesn't make a second overlay. The first stays up until 1.5 s after the last press and carries a label under the keycaps: "×2", "×3" and so on.

**When shortcuts come close together.** Overlays never overlap. A different shortcut pressed while one is showing takes over as soon as the first has had its minimum, and the first ends there. If that would show the new shortcut more than half a second late, it's left out, and a sheet says how many were.

## The Shortcuts track

Overlays go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when that track is usable, and otherwise on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. To be usable, the track must:

- be in front of every selected clip's track
- be unlocked and shown
- not be a [matte](/canvas/mattes/)
- have nothing on it from the first overlay's start to the last overlay's end

## Change an overlay

Each overlay is an ordinary graphic clip. Move, trim or delete it on the timeline, and change its keys, label, theme, position or accent colour in its [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). To change them all at once, select them first.

The overlays are drawn by the project's own copy of the bundled [Keyboard keys template](/graphics/templates/). Frame Job writes that copy into the project's graphics the first time something is placed, and reuses it after. If you've [edited that copy](/graphics/edit-a-module/), it leaves your version alone and writes a fresh one beside it for new overlays.

Undo takes the clips away but not the copy, which stays in the project's graphics for next time.

## What the sheet tells you

An informational sheet comes up when something didn't go as asked. Only the "too close" sheet comes with a change to the project.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added." | The part of the recording that plays holds no shortcut. Check that the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** on. |
| "1 shortcut came too close to show." | The overlays were added, without that many. With more it reads "3 shortcuts came too close to show." |
| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play forward." | Frame Job won't place overlays for a reversed clip. |
| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
| "The project changed while the cursor files were read, so no overlay was added. Choose Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays again." | You edited the project, or opened or left a nest, while the files were being read. Nothing was added. |

## Show shortcuts when a recording lands

**Show shortcuts**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), adds the overlays by itself on a finished screen recording, at the bottom in the dark theme. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## Good to know

- Add the overlays before you run [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/). It keeps each overlay on a Shortcuts track at normal speed.
- Running the command again on the same clips doesn't replace the overlays. The Shortcuts track isn't free any more, so you get a second Shortcuts track with the same overlays on it. Undo first if you want to start over.

## With an agent

`add_shortcut_overlays` places the same overlays. An agent can also choose how long each one shows, from 0.5 to 10 s, put them at the centre or top of the picture, use the light theme, and limit them to a stretch of the timeline. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

## Related

- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
